tasks.description:
**Antonio, driving, 2026-08-13:** *"Because we have back and forth binding last pane and last ws it would be useful to highlight the last visited pane or ws so that we know exactly where back and forth lead. A very subtle difference if possible."*

# STATE — the widget + theme half is BUILT and green; the app wiring is NOT

Uncommitted on `feat/palette-modes`, on top of `e7f30ad`. Workspace tests green, clippy 0 warnings.

## Done

- **`Theme::previous_wash_alpha`** (`heca-theme/src/theme.rs`, beside `active_wash_alpha`), defaulting to `0.05` — half the active wash, so the hint sits a clear step below the container it lives in. Per theme: grid_tron `0.05`, mocha `0.05`, latte `0.04`.

The state to read already exists and already drives the bindings — **do not derive a second history**:
- `AppState::last_visited_pane_per_ws: Vec<Option<PaneId>>` (`app_state.rs:779`), read by `handle_focus_toggle_local` (`handlers.rs:85`).
- `AppState::last_visited_ws_idx: Option<usize>` (:777), read by `handle_focus_toggle_global` (:100), maintained on workspace removal (:1290).

Three call sites:

1. **`providers/workspaces/mod.rs::pane_card`** (:739) already takes `active_pane: Option<PaneId>` and compares `active_pane == Some(pane.pane_id)` (:755). Add a `previous_pane: Option<PaneId>` beside it and call `.previous(previous_pane == Some(pane_id))` on the `Row` (:947). The function already carries `#[expect(clippy::too_many_arguments)]`; follow where `active_pane` is threaded from and thread this the same way rather than inventing a route.
2. **The workspace `DockFrame`** (`column_view` / `build_workspaces_container` area, :1140) — `.previous(ws_idx == last_visited_ws_idx)`.
3. **`chrome/expose/pane_card.rs`** — the map is where "where would I land" is most useful. `PaneCard` takes plain data, so add a `previous: bool` property and set it in `WorkspaceRow` from a value `ExposeGrid` carries down, resolved once in `register` from `last_visited_pane_per_ws`.

Bind through the signal (`previous_state()`) in `sync_chrome_signals` if the sidebar flips it without a rebuild, exactly as `active_state()` is bound.

- The last-visited pane is very often **also** the cursor's row or the selected row — that is the normal case, not an edge one. All four states must stack on one row and stay separable; the fill/edge split is what pays for that and must not be spent.
- `last_visited_ws_idx` is `None` on a fresh session and after its target is deleted (:1290). Nothing marked is correct then, **not** a mark on index 0.

# What the task delivered, end to end

|---|---|---|

## The wiring (landed in `30806b9`, merged to main in PR #260)

- `Row::previous` / `DockFrame::previous` are **signal-backed** like `active` (`ChromeSignals::pane_previous` / `ws_previous`, `chrome/mod.rs:3284`/`:3294`, pushed at `providers/workspaces/mod.rs:987`/`:1237`, synced in `sync_chrome_signals`). `chrome_signature` deliberately excludes focus, so the chrome tree does not rebuild on a focus change: a plain bool read at build time freezes for the session. This cost three rounds.
- Only the **two** panes a binding leads to are marked. The other workspace's pane is that workspace's **active** pane — what `focus_toggle_global` lands on. ⚠️ `focus.rs:69` reserves `last_visited_pane_per_ws` for the same-workspace toggle and forbids workspace switches from writing it; do not "fix" the global mark by writing it there.
- A pane that has since closed leaves the mark **off** rather than on a ghost (filtered through `find_pane_workspace`).
- Both properties reachable from the SDK (`heca-view/src/build.rs`) — `every_widget_property_is_reachable_from_the_sdk` enforces RULE ZERO by the suite, not by review.

## The tuning (`0855f37`, branch `feat/back-and-forth-marks`)

The mechanism was right and Antonio still could not see it: the previous row measured **1.35–1.60:1** against the surface it sits on, which is barely a rectangle.

| | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| grid_tron previous row | 1.54:1 | 1.95:1 (`#13394e` → `#164965`) |
| mocha previous row | 1.60:1 | 1.95:1 (`#465170` → `#4f5e82`) |
| latte previous row | 1.35:1 | 1.80:1 (`#c2cadc` → `#a4afcc`) |
| latte selected row | 1.74:1 | 2.30:1 (`#a8b2cd` → `#8d9abf`) |

`PREVIOUS_LIFT` 0.24 → 0.34 (`heca-theme/src/theme.rs`), so a palette that sets none of these derives the same step from its own surface and accent. Latte's **selected** row moved because at 1.74:1 it was the weakest of the three and left `previous` nowhere to go without overtaking it — Antonio accepted that consequence.

The frame band has no room: `background 1.00 → ws-previous 1.18 → ws-active 1.29` in grid_tron and latte (mocha 1.00 → 1.51 → 1.68). The two frames are 1.07–1.11:1 apart, so they read as the same frame. The previous frame **cannot** be lifted while staying under the active one, and widening the band costs contrast for every mark drawn inside it — the failure of 2026-08-11, in the same place.

Three options were put to Antonio: widen the band; mark it by **kind** (an edge, like the cursor) rather than weight; or leave it. **He chose to leave it** — the pane mark is what you navigate by, the workspace frame is a hint. Do not reopen this without a new reason.

**Area does the work.** A wash over a *frame* and a wash over a *row* need very different strengths from the same colour. This was got wrong twice, in opposite directions: a row value used on a frame swallowed every mark inside it; half a frame's value on a row was invisible.

**Measure colours, do not judge them.** Every value that works came from a contrast calculation against that theme's own background. Every value that failed came from picking one that looked right.

**Each theme has its own identity.** latte is light — its selection goes *darker* than the page and has needed a different value at every single step. Never ship one hue three times.

tasks.title: The exposé gets its own peek: a surface-bound key shows a letter on every card
tasks.description:
**Antonio, 2026-08-13:** *"in exposé when clicking `s` (configurable binding) keyhint to peek among all panes should be shown."*

Built, then reopened twice by what building it exposed. **Uncommitted on `main`.** Workspace green (28 binaries), clippy 0 warnings.

# 1. The feature — the map's cards are pick targets

`chrome/expose/pane_card.rs` — the card is wrapped in `KeyHint` with `.on_peek(choose)`. One line; `PaneCard::build` now returns `(KeyHint, GridCell)`.

⚠️ **The card must fill its wrapper.** `KeyHint` hugs its child, so the share or rect the parent handed the wrapper has to be passed on: `.width(Pct(1.0)).height(Pct(1.0))` on the `Row`. Without it every card collapsed to the width of the word inside it — caught by the exposé's own box test. The identical trap hit `KeyHintGroup` around the grid.

# 2. THE BUG THIS EXPOSED — the letters were invisible

Antonio: *"KeyHints are not visible. I suspect they are rendered below the overlay."* He was right, and it was not the layer stack.

**Everything checked out in isolation and the pixels were still lost.** Verified by test, not inference: `s` resolved to the action; the map's tree returned `Handled::No` for both `TextInput("s")` and `Key('s')`, so it did not swallow it; the cards declared 2 peeks with real bounds; `HintPick` had a handler; its policy was `Global`; the eligible count equalled the map's own target count; and a trace showed the letters being drawn at correct coordinates.

**The cause: a `Scene` has two halves, flushed at different times.** `render_chrome` draws `scene.base_layer()` immediately and **defers `scene.overlay_segments()` to a frame-final band** (`app/render.rs:162–166`, `render_overlay_band`), ordered by nesting **depth**. The exposé's root is an `Overlay`, which paints through `cx.with_overlay`, so the whole map lives in that band. `paint_peek_letters` built a plain `PaintCx`, so the caps went into the base — drawn *under* the map.

Same class as T416 (then it was the wrong *scene*; this was the right scene, wrong *half*), and the first fix — wrapping the caps in `cx.with_overlay` — was **also wrong**: segments sort by depth, so a plugin's overlay nesting a menu or a tooltip (depth 2) would draw over a depth-1 cap and be invisible again.

# 3. THE REAL FIX — the widget draws its own letter

**A host cannot know which half of which scene a widget it has never seen paints into, so it must not try.**

- `Base::peek_label: Signal<Option<String>>`, beside `Base::peek`. `KeyHint` paints its cap from it, in its own paint — correct segment by construction, at any depth, on any surface.
- `heca_grid_ui::offer_peek(root, path, label)` / `clear_peeks(root)` — the host's whole drawing half is *assigning* letters.
- `chrome::offer_peek_letters` / `clear_peek_letters`; `handle_hint_pick` offers on entry, `handle_hint_pick_mode` clears on every exit (before firing, since a pick may tear the tree down).
- **`paint_peek_letters` and `collect_peek_targets` are DELETED**, and `app/render.rs` carries a comment saying why no host pass may paint a keycap.
- `KeyHint::hint()` now writes `base.peek_label` — one signal, so the universal picker and a host mode (pane-select, swap) cannot show different letters over one target.
- The compact-target rule (a cap too big for an icon button goes *below* it, smaller) moved from the deleted host pass into `KeyHint::is_compact` / `keycap_rect`, in units of the inherited font. The six `HINT_*` constants in `chrome/mod.rs` are gone.

# 4. WHAT ANTONIO THEN ASKED FOR — and chose

*"suppose i'm a plugin author… I write a new overlay and add the KeyHint. what happens?"* Two things were host-only, and he chose to fix both.

## Gap 1 — the picker itself: `KeyHintGroup` (BUILT)

`heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/key_hint_group.rs`. A picker **you can declare**, over a subtree you choose:

```rust
KeyHintGroup::new(subtree).open_when(sig).on_action("mypanel.pick", move || sig.set(true))
```

While open it letters its own descendants' peek declarations (`Base::peek_label`, drawn by each widget), holds focus — that is the whole of taking the keyboard — and on the next `TextInput` fires that declaration and closes. Claims the letter in **capture**, because the regions a picker covers commonly answer typed characters themselves (the map's cards take `x`/`r`/`d`). Dismissal is the shared `[keys.widgets]` vocabulary, so it names no key. 6 tests.

The host keeps exactly one thing, because only it can answer it: **which surfaces are eligible** at screen scope. `prefix+/` is this behaviour with that filter; a plugin's is the same behaviour scoped to its own panel.

## Gap 2 — a layer could not declare an action (BUILT, Antonio chose option **b**)

A `Provider` declares actions (`actions()` + `perform()`); a **layer had no such seam**, so an overlay could only bind verbs the app had compiled in. That is why the map had to borrow the built-in `hint_pick`.

Chosen: **actions are declared on the widget**, beside `peek` and `context_menu`.

- `Base::actions: Vec<DeclaredAction>` (`{ name, run }`), `ComponentExt::on_action(name, f)`.
- `heca_grid_ui::collect_actions` / `fire_action(root, name)` — **the name is the address**, so nothing goes stale when a tree is rebuilt between a binding being read and the key pressed. First declaration in document order wins.
- `chrome::fire_widget_action(state, name)` walks visible layers front-to-back, then chrome, then pane headers.
- `dispatch_view_intent` tries it as **step 2**, between built-ins and the provider catalog. **Reachability is the gate**: only *visible* trees are walked, so an unmounted surface's verb resolves to nothing exactly as an unmounted provider's does — it needs no policy of its own because it cannot be reached off screen.

## The map now owns its picker

`PICK_ACTION = "heca.expose.pick"`, declared on the `KeyHintGroup` that wraps the map's grid. `keybindings.default.toml`: `pick = "s"` under `[[keys.surface]] heca.expose` — was `hint_pick = "s"`.

Two guard tests hold the halves together, because either alone is silent: `the_map_owns_its_picker_and_every_card_is_a_target` and `the_shipped_defaults_bind_the_maps_own_pick_action` (a name no widget declares binds fine and does nothing — indistinguishable from a typo).

# OPEN — needs Antonio

1. **NOT DRIVEN.** Nothing since the letters-invisible fix has been seen on screen. Rebuild and check: `s` on the map letters every card including floats; typing one lands there; Esc puts them away; `prefix+/` still works everywhere else; **the small pane-header action buttons** still get their caption below the icon (that rule moved into `KeyHint` and its threshold is now font-relative, so it is the most likely visual change).

tasks.title: REGRESSION — Esc no longer releases the keyboard from a focused dock back to the scrolling area
tasks.description:
**Antonio, driving, 2026-08-13:** *"when entering with `prefix+/` in a sidebar pane list I can go up and down, focus pane and select them. However I'm not able to exit without selecting anything. I should be able to do Esc and go back to normal in the scrolling area. Similarly `prefix+e` (sidebar mode) Esc should get back to the scrolling area. This behavior used to work."*

# THE CAUSE — found 2026-08-13, statically, not by guessing

**A global binding ate the key before the focused dock could see it.**

1. `keybindings.default.toml:147` — `close_overlay = ["Escape", "q", "Ctrl+q"]`, in the top-level `[keys]` table.
2. `app/registry.rs:358` — a key without `prefix+` is bound into the **`global`** layer.
3. `app/input.rs:72` — in Normal mode the `global` layer resolved **first** and, on a hit, dispatched and returned unconditionally.
4. `app/input.rs:109` — the focused-container branch, holding the Escape floor (`Escape → UnfocusDock`), was only reached if global **missed**.

So with a dock focused and no overlay open: Escape → global `close_overlay` → `handle_close_overlay` finds no top modal → returns → key consumed. `focus_layer_action` never ran. The doc comment on `handle_close_overlay` stated the false assumption out loud: *"No overlay up is a no-op, which is what makes binding Escape to it harmless."* Consuming the key **is** the harm.

**Timing confirms it:** the bare `Escape` entered `close_overlay` on 2026-08-05 (`584918c`), after "focus is the mode" landed 2026-07-29 (`69b4158`). Not the `[[keys.component]]` work, though it arrived in the same stretch.

Both filed hypotheses were wrong, and neither needed instrumenting: `focused_container()` was fine, and `[keys.widgets] dismiss` is not on this path at all — the widget-keymap route in `app/events.rs:155` only runs when `top_modal(state).is_some()`, and a focused dock is not a modal layer.

# WHAT WAS BUILT — the rule, not a patch (Antonio's call, 2026-08-13)

Antonio: *"esc should work on the focused layer… allowing to specify different action based on the focus surface"*, *"I want esc to close the current component: context_menu, command_palette, overlay, DockView etc. and go back to where we were. like in any other application. for the app most of the time the foreground component is scrolling area with panes."*

**A key acts on the surface in front of you.** Three surfaces, front to back — a **layer**, a focused **dock**, and `heca.panes` (the scrolling area) — exactly one holds the keyboard. One order for every key:

> the focused surface's own `[[keys.surface]]` entry → the **floor** its kind is guaranteed → the global `[keys]` map → then swallowed (layer, dock) or sent to the pane (`heca.panes`).

Nearest declaration wins, so a surface key now shadows a global one of the same combo — the deliberate precedence change.

**The floors are `Escape`, and neither is removable:**

| surface | Escape means |
|---|---|
| layer | `close_overlay` — it closes itself |
| dock | `unfocus_dock` — the keyboard goes back |
| `heca.panes` | **nothing** — it reaches the program in the pane, so vim still works |

## The code

- `app/input.rs` — `FocusedSurface` (Layer/Dock/Panes) + `focused_surface(state)` reducing `AppState` to it, and **`surface_action`**, a **pure** function of plain data that is the rule. Both key routes use it: the direct one and the prefix fall-through. `focus_layer_action` is gone, folded into it.
- `app/input.rs` — new constants `LAYER_FLOOR` (`"layer"`) and `PANES_SURFACE` (`"heca.panes"`).
- `app/registry.rs` — `assert_escape_floor`, one helper for both floors, replacing the inline `if name == FOCUS_LAYER` block. The `layer` floor is created even when nothing declares that mode (a layer is entered by being shown, never by a key), and is added to `UNTRIGGERED_MODES`.
- `keybindings.default.toml` — `close_overlay = ["q", "Ctrl+q"]`; `Escape` removed with the reason written down. The `[[keys.surface]]` header documents the three surfaces, the order and the floors.
- `AGENTS.md` § Keybinding Style — the rule, as a framework rule agents keep re-deriving.

## Tests

`app/input.rs` (new module, 5 tests, headless — the rule is pure, so it needed no window): Escape releases a focused dock; Escape closes the layer in front; Escape in the scrolling area is `None` (the assertion that fails if anyone gives the panes a floor "for symmetry"); a surface's own keys beat its floor and a key it does not claim falls through; a dock resolves at placement then kind.

`app/registry.rs` (2 new): the layer floor exists built from nothing, with no trigger; and **`Escape` is never a global binding**, while `q` still is.

Whole workspace green (28 suites), clippy 0 warnings with `--all-targets --all-features`.

# VERIFICATION — Antonio drives, NOT verified yet

1. `prefix+e`, then Esc → the keyboard is back in the scrolling area.
2. `prefix+/`, pick a sidebar row, then Esc without choosing → same.
3. `prefix+o` (exposé), Esc → the map closes. And `q` → still closes it.
4. In a pane, run vim, press Esc → vim gets it.
5. A context menu / the command palette, Esc → closes just that, leaving what was under it.

tasks.title: Hint 1 — the framework draws the letter, not KeyHint
tasks.description:
Read docs/hint-architecture.md first, section 7 step 1. It holds the whole design. This task is the first of six and nothing else can start until it is done.

WHAT IS WRONG NOW
Only one widget knows how to draw a letter over something: KeyHint (heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/key_hint.rs). So anything that wants a letter has to be wrapped in a KeyHint. That wrapping is the root of every other problem in this set.

WHAT SHOULD HAPPEN
Any widget can hold a letter already — Base::hint_label carries it. Drawing it is the same work no matter who asked, so the drawing moves into component::paint_child, the shared helper that containers already call. Then a widget draws its own letter and needs no wrapper.

HOW
- Take the letter drawing out of KeyHint::paint and put it in component::paint_child, reading Base::hint_label.
- Draw inside cx.with_overlay, or a widget drawn later covers the letter. Letters are flushed at the end of the frame in nesting order (heca/src/app/render.rs:162-166) — this is why the earlier attempt to fix it from the app side failed.
- Read cx.viewport(), NOT Base::viewport. Base::viewport is written per tree, so inside a pane header it reports the header's own box, and letters flipped upward and got cut off.

WATCH OUT
- Pane and DockFrame draw their children their own way instead of using the shared helper. Check both, or their letters disappear.
- KeyHint stays, but only as an option for things that are not widgets. It stops being required.
- HintPlacement mostly stops being needed once a widget places its own letter. TopLeft is in use by the exposé cards today.
- render.rs has a comment saying the app must never draw a letter itself. Keep that true.

HOW TO KNOW IT WORKS
By looking at it. Tests passing means nothing here. Antonio drives: pane headers, the dock, sidebar rows, exposé cards.

---
**Completion summary:**
DONE 2026-08-17. Uncommitted on main. Verified on screen by Antonio: prefix+q letters both sidebars, prefix+/ works, the exposé's `s` works. 28 suites green, clippy clean on --all-targets --all-features.

WHAT SHIPPED
- The four knobs that were private fields on KeyHint (placement, size, colour, offset_y) became HintStyle, carried on Base as `Base::hint_style` (heca-grid-ui/src/component.rs). KeyHint's builders write into it.
- The keycap geometry left KeyHint as free functions in heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/key_hint.rs: hint_font, is_compact, keycap_rect, plus paint_hint_label, which does the drawing.
- component::paint_child (heca-grid-ui/src/component.rs:932) calls paint_hint_label after painting the child. Both hard-won rules kept and documented there: the viewport comes from the PAINT context (not Base::viewport, which is per tree and made caps flip and clip inside a pane header), and the cap goes into the overlay band via cx.with_overlay.
- KeyHint keeps on_hint and stays as a decorator for regions that are not widgets; its paint is now only "paint the child".

WHAT THE TASK DID NOT PREDICT
- Pane and DockFrame were already fine. The real problem was 13 OTHER containers calling child.paint(cx) directly and so skipping the framework: Button, Row, Card, Item, Tag, Choice, Grid, Tabs, Select, RailCell, IconButton, Visibility, CommandPalette. All routed through paint_child.
- paint_child was pub(crate), so heca's own container in chrome/mod.rs hand-rolled the loop and a plugin writing a container could not have drawn its children correctly at all. Now `pub` and exported from lib.rs.
- A root widget's own letter never drew (collect_hints offers one to the root too). The surface roots in chrome/mod.rs go through paint_child now.

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE WORTH KNOWING: those 13 containers now skip children marked hidden, which they did not before. Layout collapses hidden nodes to zero size at the top-left, so painting them was stamping stale content; skipping matches every other container.

TESTS: `any_widget_carrying_a_letter_gets_a_keycap_not_only_key_hint` (heca-grid-ui/tests/phase_a.rs) — a bare Label with no KeyHint anywhere gets its letter drawn. The pre-existing key_hint_overlays_letter_only_when_set was pointed at paint_child, since calling paint directly is painting around the framework.

BUG FOUND AND FIXED WHILE DRIVING THIS (separate from the task, in the previous session's uncommitted work): offer_hint_by_key's walk used .any(), which stops at the first match, so a pane listed in BOTH sidebars was lettered only in the left one. Traced with a temporary diagnostic (since removed) that printed `nodes naming it: chrome=2` while one letter was handed out. Fixed to visit every child; `||` short-circuits too, so it is a loop. Guarded by `a_target_listed_in_two_places_is_lettered_in_both`. label_nearest keeps its .any() on purpose (nearest single declaration within one named row), and offer_in_every_tree keeps its early return across trees (a surface in front shadows one behind).

OPEN, NOT A BUG: the same pane shown in both sidebars wears the SAME letter in both. That is correct — the letter names the pane, not the row. Antonio flagged he may not like seeing it twice; if so the decision is to letter only the sidebar holding the keyboard, and that needs writing up separately.

tasks.title: Hint 4 — on_hint becomes the override, and a pick becomes a real event
tasks.description:
Hint 4 — `on_hint` becomes the override, and a pick becomes a real event.

✅ **DONE 2026-08-21**, driven and confirmed by Antonio, committed as `26e5cee`.

═══ WHAT SHIPPED ═══

**1. `on_hint` is on every widget.** `ComponentExt::on_hint` (`heca-grid-ui/src/builders.rs`), beside `on_click`. `KeyHint::on_hint` is **deleted**; `KeyHint` stays as a decorator for a region that is not a widget you can put a builder on. Call sites read identically.

**2. The pick is a real event.** `Event::Hint(HintEvent { key, bounds })` + `EventKind::Hint`, delivered through the existing `deliver_to_path` — capture down, target, bubble up. `fire_hint` no longer calls the closure; it builds the event and delivers it.

**3. Target phase only.** `component::run_pick` runs the declaration (or the widget's own click) in the target arm of `deliver_to_path`. A pickable container holding pickable rows lands on the row.

**4. Delegation.** The bubbled `Event::Hint` — `.on(EventKind::Hint, …)` sees which widget was picked and can `stop_propagation`. It declares nothing and gets no letter. `stop_propagation` stops **outer** listeners hearing it; it does not un-run the target, because the target phase already happened.

**5. A pick carries its `Intent`, and a refused pick gets no letter.** `Base::hint` is now `hint::Hint { intent: Option<heca_view::Intent>, run }`. `heca-grid-ui` took a dependency on `heca-view` (serde-only, zero deps — not a cycle, nothing moved) so the declaration can name the act. The library stores it and never reads it.

═══ THE FILTER, AND WHY IT IS SHAPED THIS WAY ═══

`chrome::active_hint_targets` → `candidate_allowed` asks **one question of every candidate on every surface**: what do you do? It takes the `Intent` off the declaration and asks `route_interaction`. **No `state.panes`, no key resolution, no list of kinds** — Antonio, 2026-08-21: *"this is a behavior that should work for every widget, component present and future. NO HARDCODED to pane, ws or other stuff."* An earlier version resolved a candidate's identity back to the pane that owns it; it was removed, along with `nav::key_at_path` which existed only for it.

Two supporting pieces, both centralized:
- **The source comes from the emitter.** `ChromeIntentEmitter` is a struct carrying the `InteractionSource` it stamps (`source()` / `fire()`); `RetainedChrome` stores `emit.source()`; `chrome/hint/targets.rs::pick_source` reads it off the surface. The filter asking as `Keyboard` while the chrome tree dispatches as `MouseLeftSidebar` resolved to different domains — the picker offered letters in `Container` that execution refused in `Floating`. 24 call sites moved from `emit(x)` to `emit.fire(x)`.
- **A chrome button's pick is named where its tooltip is** (`action_tooltip`, `chrome/pane_header.rs`). A button hands over one closure for click and pick; a closure is opaque, so every chrome button escaped the filter and the sidebar toggles wore letters while `sidebar_left` was already refused.

**The declaration's half.** `ActionMeta.policy` is required with no permissive default; an action that misdescribes itself is the one thing no mechanism can correct. `workspaces.peek_selected` and `workspaces.activate_selected` both declared `Global` while both end by focusing a pane — they now share one named constant `reaches_a_pane = ActionPolicy::SourceDependent`, so the rule has one name and no copy is left behind.

**Known coarseness:** the active float's own *sidebar rows* lose their letters too, though focusing that pane would be permitted — `SourceDependent` has no introspectable `WmAction` behind a name-keyed verb, so the router takes its conservative branch. Making it precise means the row declaring the composite it performs.

═══ FILES ═══
- `heca-grid-ui/src/hint.rs` → **`hint/`** (declaration · collect · fire · offer · actions · tests · mod)
- `heca/src/chrome/hint.rs` → **`hint/`** (letters · surfaces · visibility · targets · mod)
- `heca-grid-ui/src/{builders,component,event,lib,nav}.rs`, `heca-grid-ui/Cargo.toml`
- `heca/src/chrome/{mod,pane_header,overlay,palette,context_menu,expose/mod}.rs`, `heca/src/chrome/pane/shell.rs`
- `heca/src/app/{interaction,render}.rs`, `heca/src/providers/{mod,workspaces/*}.rs`, `heca-view-realize/src/lib.rs`
- `docs/hint-architecture.md`, `docs/widgets.md`

═══ TESTS ═══
`heca-grid-ui/src/hint/tests.rs`: only the picked widget runs its declaration · a listening container sees which child was picked and gets no letter · a listener can stop a pick going further up.
`heca/src/chrome/pane/shell.rs`: the pane says what picking it would do.
`heca/src/chrome/pane_header.rs`: a button's pick is named from its action · a pick that already named itself is left alone.
`heca/src/app/interaction.rs`: a pick that would be refused resolves to a refused action.
Gates: heca 579 · heca-grid-ui 256 · view-realize 67 · core 96 · config 83 · renderer 40 · theme 25 · view 20 · clippy clean. Standing gate: `./scripts/lint-changed.sh test`.

═══ STILL OPEN ═══
- **The two-direction search in `offer_hint_by_key`** (this task's DELETES). Only removable once the app's declarations move off their `KeyHint` wrappers onto the widgets — the wrapper carries the **placement** (`Base::hint_style`, whose builders are `KeyHint`'s), so moving them without a placement builder on `ComponentExt` silently relocates every keycap. Goes with **T438**.
- **`SidebarLeft`/`SidebarRight` are `TiledOnly`** (`app/interaction.rs:385`, `:398`) — deliberate and documented, so the toggles are refused while floating and now correctly get no letter. **DECIDED 2026-08-21: it stays.** Antonio, raising it a second time: *"i've said to leave the sidebar hint as is now."* Do not re-open it.
- **One pane, three letters.** `target_identity` prefixes the identity with its surface (T445: *"two surfaces may each hold a pane:7 and they are not the same pickable thing"*), so `prefix+/` treats a float and its two sidebar rows as three targets, while `offer_hint_by_key` gives one pane one letter everywhere (`a_target_listed_in_two_places_is_lettered_in_both`). The two pickers disagree. Raised with Antonio 2026-08-21, left as-is.
- **File splits found while doing this:** filed as **T468**.

tasks.title: Hint 5 — the app chooses the letters, and there is always exactly one
tasks.description:
Read docs/hint-architecture.md sections 2a and 6.

TWO THINGS, BOTH DECIDED.

1. ONE LETTER. ALWAYS. (Antonio, 2026-08-17: "typing 2 letters is not an option. always 1. stay with 52.")
A pick is one keystroke. Not a sequence you type and narrow, not a first letter then a second. a-z then A-Z is 52, and past 52 a target gets no letter. DO NOT PROPOSE TWO-KEY SEQUENCES AGAIN — it has been raised and refused, and vimium doing it is not an argument. Anything needing more than 52 at once is a SCOPE problem: the picker covers too much, and the answer is a smaller picker (a surface's own, see T436), never a longer keystroke.
The 52 cap already exists in the link picker (heca/src/app/terminal_host.rs:783, "return hints; // 52-label cap reached"). Keep that behaviour. A target with no letter is not an error, but make sure it does not read as a broken picker either.

2. THE APP CHOOSES WHICH LETTERS, NOT THE LIBRARY.
heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/key_hint_group.rs:51 fixes the alphabet inside the library:
  fn letters() -> impl Iterator<Item = char> { ('a'..='z').chain('A'..='Z') }
That is a choice about how THIS app hands out letters, sitting inside a widget other people are meant to reuse. Someone else cannot ask for home-row first, cannot use a different layout, and cannot keep a letter free for closing the picker. Let the caller pass the letters in; keep today's a-z then A-Z as the default so nothing that already works changes.

WHERE THE LINE IS
- library: Base::hint, Base::hint_label, on_hint, drawing the letter, the picker widget itself.
- app (heca/src/chrome/hint.rs): which letters, in what order, who is left out — including the rule that the pane you are already on gets none, and remembering which letters you handed out so you take back only your own.

WATCH OUT: the picker takes its closing key from [keys.widgets] so it never names a key itself. The new letter source must not quietly reserve one again.

TEST: a picker given its own letters uses them, in that order. Never more than one keystroke per pick.

---
**Completion summary:**
DONE 2026-08-17, on branch feat/hint-anything-actionable (not yet committed). 1339 tests pass, clippy clean on --all-targets --all-features. No visual check needed — this changes where the alphabet lives, not what is drawn; the letters are byte-identical to before.

WHAT SHIPPED
- heca_grid_ui::widgets::DEFAULT_LETTERS — a public const, the one place the order lives. Its doc carries the one-letter/52-cap rule and the refusal of two-key sequences.
- KeyHintGroup::letters(impl IntoIterator<Item = char>) — the caller's alphabet, in the caller's order. Marked host_only ("an app's choice of alphabet, not data a described tree carries"). Default is DEFAULT_LETTERS, so no existing call site changes behaviour. The hardcoded fn letters() -> ('a'..='z').chain('A'..='Z') at key_hint_group.rs:51 is gone.
- The app's own copy is gone too: heca/src/app/selection.rs held a 52-entry CANDIDATE_ALPHABET array. candidate_letter now reads DEFAULT_LETTERS. That was the second copy of one decision, and the reason home-row ordering would otherwise have had to be applied twice.

THE CAP IS NOW THE ALPHABET, not a separate number
PANE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT = DEFAULT_LETTERS.len() instead of a literal 52. The three collectors in selection.rs stopped indexing the array behind a hand-written guard: collect_all_pane_candidates uses `let Some(ch) = candidate_letter(len) else { return }`, and collect_workspace_candidates / collect_column_candidates zip DEFAULT_LETTERS.chars(), which caps at its length by construction. Four unguarded index sites became impossible to get wrong.

TESTS (heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/key_hint_group.rs)
- the_caller_chooses_the_letters_and_their_order
- running_out_of_letters_gives_none_rather_than_a_longer_one — a target past the end gets None, never a second keystroke
- the_default_alphabet_is_fifty_two_single_keystrokes

CONSEQUENCE FOR T443: home row is now a one-line reorder of DEFAULT_LETTERS, and every picker in both crates follows. Doing this first was the point.

tasks.title: Hint 6 — write the failing test first, before the plugin work
tasks.description:
Read docs/hint-architecture.md sections 7 step 4 and 9.

THE RULE THIS PROTECTS
Anything a widget can do in Rust, a plugin must be able to ask for in JSON. So: every widget that can be given a hint in code must also accept a hint written into its ViewNode. The two ways of saying the same thing must not drift apart.

WRITE IT FAILING, AND WRITE IT BEFORE T435 AND T436.
Leave it red on purpose. T435 and T436 are what make it pass. Written afterwards it would only describe what was built, which protects nothing.

HOW
There is already a test called every_widget_property_is_reachable_from_the_sdk. Find it and copy its shape: go through the widgets, and for each one that supports a hint in Rust, check it also accepts a hint in its ViewNode.

WHY A TEST AND NOT A NOTE IN A DOCUMENT
The most important rule in this project is written in three separate places. It was read three times in one day and still broken the same day. Writing it down again does not work. A test that fails does.

Do not soften the check to make it pass early. Red until the feature exists is the whole point.

---
**Completion summary:**
✅ DONE 2026-08-21. Two tests in `heca-view-realize/src/lib.rs`:

**`every_kind_can_be_given_a_hint_from_the_sdk`** — the guard, **written red on purpose**. Walks `WidgetKind::ALL`, reads `heca-view/src/build.rs`'s `with_event!` table (the one place a builder gets its event setters), and fails naming every kind that takes a hint natively — `ComponentExt::on_hint` is on every widget since T432 — but cannot be given one through the typed SDK. Red at 25 kinds; `ScrollBar` is the only excusal, with its reason (host-only, `realize` refuses it). It reads source rather than calling it, because *"does a method exist"* is not a question a running test can ask — the same technique as `every_widget_property_is_reachable_from_the_sdk`.

**`a_hint_written_into_any_kind_is_found_by_the_picker`** — passes, and locks the wire-level half: every kind realized with a `hint` intent is found by `fire_hint` and fires that intent. So T435 is only about *reach*, not about whether the capability works.

**Found while doing it — a pre-existing red the session's gates had been missing.** `every_widget_property_is_reachable_from_the_sdk` was failing on `Row::previous_tint`, added by `a0cd8c7` with no SDK setter. Fixed here (`heca-view/src/build.rs`; `with_props` applies it generically, so the setter is not a dead end). It failed unnoticed because the gate all session was `cargo test -p heca-grid-ui -p heca`, which never runs this crate — **the standing gate is now `./scripts/lint-changed.sh test`** (agreed with Antonio 2026-08-21), which maps changed files to crates and is scoped *and* complete.

Gates: heca 579 · grid-ui 256 · core 96 · config 83 · renderer 40 · theme 25 · view 20 · view-realize 64 pass + 1 intended red.

tasks.title: Hint 7 — a plugin can say "this can be picked" in JSON
tasks.description:
Read docs/hint-architecture.md section 7 step 5. Do T432 and T434 first. This turns part of T434's failing test green.

WHY THIS IS THE IMPORTANT ONE
This is the half that plugins actually need. A plugin cannot hand us a Rust function, so without this it can draw a row but can never make that row pickable. The JSON spelling is not a convenience, it is the feature.

WHAT IT SHOULD LOOK LIKE
  { "kind": "Row",
    "props":  { "nav_key": "docker:abc" },
    "events": { "hint": { "action": "docker.restart", "args": { "id": "abc" } } } }

HOW
realize connects that hint entry to on_hint, firing the named action. Two other events, press and change, already work exactly this way. Find them and follow the same shape. Do not invent a second pattern.

BOTH WAYS OF WRITING IT END UP IN THE SAME PLACE — Base::hint. One door. Two separate paths handling the same thing always drift apart somewhere the tests cannot see.

Nothing new is needed to identify the row: it uses its own nav_key, which already travels as JSON. No registry, no ids to hand out and take back, nothing private to the app in any signature.

WATCH OUT
- The rule from T432 must hold here too: a plugin's nested pickable rows behave the same as ours, so only the row actually picked runs its action.
- A plugin must also be able to listen for picks from its children, or it gets half the model.
- A plugin already learns which letters are on screen through hint.changed, which is built.

---
**Completion summary:**
✅ DONE 2026-08-21 — turns T434's guard green.

**`heca-view/src/build.rs`: `on_hint` is now on every kind in the `with_event!` table**, not seven. Natively a hint is `ComponentExt::on_hint` — universal, on `Base`, no widget opts in (T432) — and `realize` writes a node's `hint` event into that same slot for every kind, in the common path rather than a per-kind arm. The SDK was the only place the capability stopped, so an author writing a `Label`, a `Card` or a `Panel` could draw the thing and never make it pickable while the identical tree written as a raw `ViewNode` could.

A hint is enough on its own: a node carrying one **is** a target, clickable or not (`hint::is_target` = `hintable && (hint.is_some() || actionable)`). `press` stays only on the kinds `realize` wires a click for — a `press` on a `Separator` would be a setter that silently does nothing. `ScrollBar` is absent from the table and from the SDK: host-only, `realize` refuses it.

**Tests** (`heca-view-realize`): `a_plugin_can_make_anything_pickable_from_the_sdk` — a `build::Label` with a hint is found and fires the plugin's own intent, arguments and all; `a_described_pick_lands_on_the_node_it_named_and_not_its_container` — T432's target-phase rule holds for a described tree, so a plugin's nested pickable rows behave like heca's own.

Gates via `./scripts/lint-changed.sh test` (the new standing gate): heca 579 · grid-ui 256 · view-realize 67 · core 96 · config 83 · renderer 40 · theme 25 · view 20 · 0 failed. Clippy clean.

═══ TWO GAPS FOUND, NOT CLOSED HERE ═══

1. **A described container cannot listen for picks from its children.** T435's own watch-list asks for it (*"a plugin must also be able to listen for picks from its children, or it gets half the model"*). Natively that is the bubbled `Event::Hint` — `.on(EventKind::Hint, …)`, which sees `ev.key` and can `stop_propagation`. There is **no declarative spelling**, and inventing an event name for it is a design decision, not a gap to fill quietly. A described node's own `hint` fires in the target phase only, so binding it on a container does *not* observe its children.

2. **`key` is on the SDK's shared builder trait but `Label` cannot reach it** — `build::Label::new("x").key("docker:abc")` does not compile. Identity is universal on `Base` and required for a letter to stay with its target between openings (T445), so this is the same shape of gap this task just closed for `hint`. Not investigated further; worth its own task.

tasks.title: Hint 8 — a plugin can own a picker, not just be picked
tasks.description:
Read docs/hint-architecture.md section 7 step 6. Last of the six. Turns the rest of T434's failing test green.

THE GAP
After T435 a plugin can mark things as pickable. It still cannot open a picker of its own — the thing that shows the letters and reads the keystroke. That ability just became easy for our own code and would be left impossible for everyone else. Antonio asked for "the builder plus its ViewNode", meaning both halves, always.

WHAT TO BUILD
1. KeyHintGroup becomes something a ViewNode can create (heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/key_hint_group.rs, 6 tests today).
2. on_action gets its JSON form too, so a plugin can name an action the way the exposé owns heca.expose.pick, bound to "s".

KEEP WHAT IT ALREADY DOES RIGHT
It letters only what is beneath it. It holds the keyboard. It grabs the letter on the way down, which is what lets the exposé cards answer x, r and d themselves. It takes its closing key from [keys.widgets] so it never names a key. The JSON form must lose none of this.

THE TEST TO APPLY BEFORE CALLING IT DONE
Write out the line a plugin author would actually type. If it needs a registry, an id, or a type that only this app can see, then the API is missing something — it is not the author's problem to work around. HintTargetRegistry, HintTargets, HintTargetId, Base::hint_target and named_press were all removed for this reason and must not come back.

WHEN THIS IS DONE
Everything a plugin author writes is either a builder on their own widget or a string in their own JSON.

---
**Completion summary:**
✅ DONE 2026-08-23 — visual check passed (Antonio drove the exposé picker: `s` letters the cards, typing one jumps). Branch feat/hint-anything-actionable, NOT committed.

WHAT A PLUGIN AUTHOR WRITES NOW
  KeyHintGroup::new(panel).opens_on("mypanel.pick")                        // native
  { "kind": "KeyHintGroup", "props": { "opens_on": "mypanel.pick" }, ... } // described
  [[keys.surface]] name = "mypanel" / pick = "s"                           // the key, in config
No registry, no id, no host-private type, no signal, no closure. Rule Zero satisfied.

1. `KeyHintGroup::opens_on(name)` (heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/key_hint_group.rs). The picker's three native parts — a signal, `open_when` binding it, an `on_action` closure flipping it — became ONE builder. That is what made it declarable at all: static data can carry a name, never the other two. It also moves the rule "an open picker holds the keyboard" inside the widget, where a call site cannot get it half right. `open_when` stays host_only for the case where the host already owns the state.

2. `WidgetKind::KeyHintGroup` + SDK builder + `realize` arm. Its children are what it letters (one child, or a column of several — a transparent wrapper, so that is what they already were). `opens_on` arrives through the generated property surface, so the verb is the widget's own builder and not a name repeated in realize.

3. `ViewNode.actions` (name → Intent) — the declarative form of `on_action`, read ONCE in `realize` for every kind beside hint/key/hintable. `ComponentExt::on_action` is universal, so a per-kind arm would be one framework rule written 33 times. SDK setter on the shared `Style` trait. An EVENT is fired at a node by what the user did to it; an ACTION is a name said out loud by a binding/palette/RPC, answered by whoever on screen declares it. Both authoring paths land in `Base::actions` — one door.

4. One refusal, at the only place that knows both names: a verb whose intent names ITSELF is not declared. It would resolve back through the router to this same widget and re-post forever — a description spinning the event loop.

5. The exposé says `.opens_on(PICK_ACTION)` (heca/src/chrome/expose/mod.rs:206). The described picker IS the native one, not a copy.

The three existing coverage guards absorb the new kind with NO exception added.

GATES: ./scripts/lint-changed.sh test + clippy, both green. heca 579 · grid-ui 258 · view-realize 70 · core 96 · config 83 · view 20. Doc examples compile.

DECIDED, NOT CHANGED: `letters()` stays host_only — T433 decided the app chooses the alphabet, not the library and not a described tree.

Carried out of the P082 handoff so it is not lost when that handoff is archived.

WHY NOBODY HAD SEEN THEM
Where a letter sits was, until recently, ignored. The app drew every letter itself and threw away what each widget asked for. Removing that app-side drawing made every widget's request take effect at once. The sidebar asks for its letters on the right — centre-right and top-right — and those positions had never been on screen.

═══ RESULT — driven on screen by Antonio, 2026-08-24 ═══

1. NORMAL SIDEBAR ROWS (prefix+q) — OK. Letter in the right corner, fully visible, clear of the row's text. pane_row.rs:360 CenterRight, column_group.rs:81 CenterRight, workspace_frame.rs:146 TopRight + offset_y.
2. ROWS AT THE TOP AND BOTTOM EDGES — OK.
3. A SCROLLED SIDEBAR — OK. A half-visible row keeps a whole letter, nudged inside its own visible sliver; a row too far past the fold gets none.
4. A NARROW WINDOW — accepted by Antonio as it now stands ("for me its good this"), but the trace found two real defects behind the pile-up he first photographed. Both filed; neither is fixed here.
5. THE REGRESSION (the flip measuring the pane header instead of the window) — OK, did not come back.

═══ WHAT THE TRACE FOUND, AND WHAT IT DISPROVED ═══
A temporary probe in heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/key_hint.rs (paint_hint_label) printed placement / row bounds / clip / room / cap / fitted for every letter — 9060 lines. The probe has been REMOVED; `git diff heca-grid-ui/` is clean.

DISPROVED: the first hypothesis was that at narrow width the rows overflow horizontally and `fit_into_view` clamps their CenterRight caps to the fold, piling them mid-screen. The data says no: not one cap was ever moved horizontally, and every sidebar row sat entirely inside its clip (row=(32,97 248x73), room identical) at every width tested down to a 87px clip. Reasoning produced the wrong answer; one trace produced the right one, as it has every time in this phase.

FOUND — P082(F003)/T478, a zero-width pane still gets a letter:
    [hint] "p" place=Center row=(318,40 0x728) clip=none cap=(308,394)
    [hint] "v" place=Center row=(314,40 0x728) clip=none cap=(304,394)
Two sidebars at 288 each in a ~575-wide window squeeze the scrolling area to ZERO width. `Center` computes `loc.x + (w - capW)/2`, so with w=0 the cap lands half a keycap OUTSIDE the pane, and several such panes stack 4px apart in the gutter. That is exactly the pile-up in the screenshot — nothing was dragged anywhere. The defect is candidacy: a pane nobody can see should not be spending one of the 52 letters.

FOUND — P082(F003)/T479, a compact target's caption is dragged onto its icon:
    [hint] "w" place=TopCenter row=(526,48 26x25) room=(526,48 26x25) cap=(531,75) -> (531,56)
474 occurrences in one session, all TopCenter. `keycap_rect` deliberately places a compact target's cap OUTSIDE the target (below it, so the icon stays visible); `fit_into_view` then clamps it into `bounds ∩ clip` — the target itself — undoing that on the very next line. Two individually correct, individually documented rules a few lines apart in one file, composing into a wrong one. Width-independent; nothing tested it.

ALSO SEEN, not filed (layout, not hints): at that width the right sidebar's clip runs to x=594 in a ~575-wide window, so the workspace dock's keycap is cut in half by the window edge. Two 288-wide sidebars do not fit and nothing shrinks or hides them.

tasks.title: Hint 2 — anything actionable gets a letter, and hintable(false) opts out
tasks.description:
Read docs/hint-architecture.md sections 2 and 2b. Needs T431 first.

THE DECISION (Antonio, 2026-08-17): every actionable widget is automatically hintable, with a property to opt out. Confirmed name: .hintable(false).

Three states, and only three:
- say nothing → actionable, so it gets a letter, and picking it does what clicking it does
- .on_hint(...) → gets a letter, and picking it does THIS instead (heca's sidebar row: a click leaves the sidebar, a pick stays)
- .hintable(false) → never gets a letter, however actionable it is

HOW "ACTIONABLE" IS ANSWERED (Antonio, 2026-08-17: "we can see when prefix+/ is pressed if there is an actionable event like on_click, on_key_up etc... and if it has hintable(false). Can we?" — yes)
Handlers::has(kind) is already public (heca-grid-ui/src/event.rs:915), "the cheap check the router makes before building an event nobody wants". The walk asks each widget directly:
    actionable    = has(Click) || has(DoubleClick) || has(Key)
    gets a letter = actionable && !hintable(false)
NO NEW FLAG ON Base. An earlier plan for this phase added one so activation had a single name; it was deleted because the handler list answers it and the walk visits every widget anyway.
EventKind::Widget is deliberately NOT in the list — it covers Activate, Dismiss, ScrollPageDown and MenuUp alike, so counting it would letter every ScrollRegion.

COST: the walk runs ONCE, when the picker opens — not per frame. Afterwards each widget just reads its own signal to draw its letter. DO NOT CACHE: trees are rebuilt between frames and a cached path to a moved widget is the bug this design avoids (see fire_hint's doc — a rebuilt tree "simply offers a fresh set").

WHAT TO CHANGE
- collect_hints (heca-grid-ui/src/hint.rs:39) stops requiring an explicit Base::hint and takes anything actionable, minus anything marked hintable(false).
- fire_hint runs the explicit hint when there is one, otherwise the widget's own action — the same "hint, or else press" rule the declarative side has always had (heca-view-realize/src/lib.rs:638).
- .hintable(bool) on ComponentExt, with a matching "hintable" prop in ViewNode so both spellings agree.

⚠️ CORRECT docs/chrome-and-ui.md:394 IN THIS STEP. It currently says: "`.hintable(false)` was written here as the opt-out and never existed. There is nothing to opt out of." That is wrong. BACKLOG.md:1490 quotes the original design, which said the opposite — automatic for anything actionable, opt out with .hintable(false), one system for app and plugin. A previous session found the native code only did explicit opt-in and rewrote the DOCUMENTATION to match the CODE. That is how this decision was lost the first time. If that sentence survives this task it will be lost again.

KNOWN CONSEQUENCE, ACCEPTED: on_key_down and on_key_up both register as EventKind::Key and sort themselves out inside the closure (builders.rs:601), so has(Key) is also true of a widget listening only for Escape or arrows. Those get a letter too. Watch it on screen; .hintable(false) is the fix where it is wrong, not a narrower rule.

TEST: a Button with only a click handler is offered a letter with nothing declared. The same Button with .hintable(false) is not. A ScrollRegion is not.

ONE place for the generic listeners: ComponentExt::on (builders.rs) sets it for Click / DoubleClick / Key, so on_click, on_double_click, on_key_down and on_key_up are all covered without four copies. tasks.title: The identity rule is enforced — a warning, a test, and a realize-time error
tasks.description:
⭐ READ docs/widgets.md § Identity FIRST — the full record lives there.

STATUS 2026-08-19 — scope corrected. TWO of the three parts are DONE; only the ENFORCEMENT is left,
and that is now the whole of this task. (Its description previously said the automatic identity was
still to build; it had already landed and nobody updated the text.)

═══ DONE ═══
- **The rename** (commit 0a06ef5): nav_key → key, everywhere. One rename carried the family, because
  each name contained the old one: `Base::nav_key` → `Base::key`, `ComponentExt::nav_key` → `key`,
  `collect_nav_keys` → `collect_keys`, `nav_key_at` → `key_at`, and the app's pane_nav_key /
  workspace_nav_key / column_nav_key → pane_key / workspace_key / column_key. `key` was not invented:
  `CardGrid` already documented its own as "the caller's own — a pane id, a path, a codepoint".
- **The automatic identity**: `heca_grid_ui::nav::identity_of` (heca-grid-ui/src/nav.rs:141), with
  tests. Three levels, each used only when the one above is ambiguous — the widget's own name within
  the nearest keyed ancestor, then name + index among IDENTICALLY-NAMED siblings in that scope, then
  nothing. The name comes from `Component::text_summary()`. Derived from CONTENT, never position.

═══ MOVED OUT ═══
- `scope_key` → T446. It turned out NOT to be derivable from `key`, and the reason is worth keeping:
  mouse.rs:133 states a deliberate rule — "clicking a container's padding is not a request to move
  the cursor" — and merging the fields makes `key_at` return the container's own key for a padding
  click, moving the cursor to something that is not a row. The obvious repair ("a keyed node with
  keyed children is a region") fails too: the sidebar is a tree, and a workspace row contains column
  rows while being a perfectly good cursor target itself.
- The POSITIONAL ancestor keys (`ws:0`, `col:0:2`) were never part of this task, despite being
  discussed alongside it. They now have their own: see the sibling task filed 2026-08-19.

═══ STILL TO BUILD — THE ENFORCEMENT, and none of it exists ═══
A typestate builder where a collection item does not compile without a key was CONSIDERED AND
REJECTED: noise on every widget, and a plugin sending JSON never meets the Rust compiler. Instead, as
React does:

1. **A warning when a collection's children have no keys** — at the moment it can be seen and fixed.
2. **A test over heca's own chrome**, so our rows stay keyed.
3. **An error at realize time** for a plugin node declaring a `press` inside a collection with no
   `key` — the ONLY one of the three that reaches a plugin author, and therefore the important one.

Checked 2026-08-19: no warning in heca-grid-ui/src/nav.rs, no such check in heca-view-realize, and no
test over heca's chrome keys. All three are unbuilt.

═══ WHY IT MATTERS, WITH THIS WEEK'S EVIDENCE ═══
Derived identity is a floor, not a guarantee — docs/widgets.md states the limit: "a derived identity
changes if the label changes". The pane-header buttons hit exactly that: zooming changed what the
cluster rendered, so their letters moved under Antonio while he was driving (F011/P094/T451). The fix
was an explicit `.key(action_name)`, which is precisely the thing a warning would have prompted
someone to write. Nothing failed; nothing could have.

═══ NAMING, SETTLED — do not re-open ═══
`key`, not `id`: `id` suggests document-wide uniqueness the way HTML means it, while this is scoped to
its collection, which is React's meaning. And NO `Hintable…` prefix anywhere — the identity serves the
cursor, the right-click, drag AND the picker, so naming it after one of four readers would be wrong.

---
**Completion summary:**
DONE 2026-08-19. The enforcement shipped — all three pieces, plus the declarative `key` they enforce.

═══ WHAT WAS BUILT ═══

1. THE WARNING — `heca_grid_ui::nav::ambiguous_identities(&dyn Component) -> Vec<Ambiguity>` (nav.rs).
   A container with two or more children that are unkeyed, ACTIONABLE (`Base::activatable`) and
   derive the same `text_summary`. Pure data; the library prints nothing.

2. THE TESTS over heca's own chrome — two, on the two real collections, both with fixtures where
   every pane is named `zsh` so a derived identity cannot save them:
   - `providers::workspaces::tests::every_row_of_the_real_sidebar_tree_is_keyed_even_when_two_panes_share_a_name`
   - `chrome::expose::expose_grid::tests::every_card_of_the_map_is_keyed_even_when_every_pane_shares_a_name`

3. THE REALIZE-TIME ERROR — `heca_view::unkeyed_collection_items(&ViewNode) -> Vec<UnkeyedItem>`.
   A node binding `press`, with no `key`, among 2+ direct siblings of the same `WidgetKind`. It lives
   in `heca-view` (which compiles without anything that draws) so a plugin's own build can run it.

   It needed `key` on the declarative side FIRST — it did not exist. docs/widgets.md had promised it
   ("Declarative form: `key` is an ordinary prop on the node") but no code read it. `hintable` was
   the same: documented, unbuilt. Both now read GENERICALLY in `realize()`, beside style and the
   `hint` event — never a per-kind arm, because a collection can be built from any kind, so the
   identity of an item belongs to no widget's builder surface. Landed: `ViewNode::key`/`declared_key`,
   `build::Style::key`/`hintable`.

   REPORTING: `heca/src/chrome/identity.rs` (new). Each distinct finding said ONCE — a chrome tree is
   rebuilt constantly and a description is re-realized on every theme reload. Wired at
   `build_chrome_root`, `sync_pane_headers`, and both description sites in `chrome/overlay.rs`. The
   description check runs at the bridge, PER DESCRIPTION, not inside `realize` — a statement about
   the description, not about one realization of it.

═══ THE DECISION THAT MATTERS, AND THE TEST THAT FORCED IT ═══
"Only what you can act on is reported." The first version reported SEVEN findings against heca's own
sidebar, none real: a `KeyHint` wrapper inherits the row's name through `text_summary` while carrying
no key, so every wrapped row looked anonymous; and two labels inside one keyed pane row looked like a
collection. Requiring `activatable` fixes all of it, and makes both halves say the same thing (the
declarative half already asked for a `press`). Held by `inert_siblings_are_not_reported` and
`a_transparent_wrapper_around_a_keyed_row_is_not_an_item`.

Identity is what a cursor, a right-click, a drag and a remembered hint letter are kept ON — all four
need something to act on. Two labels in a row are that row's CONTENT; the row carries the key.

═══ DOCS (mandatory, both audiences) ═══
docs/widgets.md § Identity: removed the stale "the code still says nav_key/scope_key" banner (renamed
in 0a06ef5); `collect_nav_keys`/`nav_key_at` → `collect_keys`/`key_at` + added `identity_of`;
corrected the claim that `scope_key` had disappeared (it has NOT — the padding-click reason is now
recorded there, see T446). New "Identity props" section for `key`/`hintable` with both authoring
forms. "Forcing a `key`" rewritten to describe what was actually built.
AGENTS.md: four stale `nav_key` mentions → `key`.

═══ VERIFICATION ═══
26 suites · 1392 tests · 0 failed; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features` clean.
NOT driven in the GPU app — there is nothing visible to drive: the warning only prints, and it prints
nothing today because the sidebar and the exposé are already correctly keyed. That is the point of it.

tasks.title: A letter stays with its target between openings of the picker
tasks.description:
Read docs/hint-architecture.md section 2e. Needs T444 (identity) and should follow T443 (home row) — see the ordering note below.

THE REPORT (Antonio, driving, 2026-08-17): "i want to expand a pane, prefix+/ and 'k' appears on that icon. I press k and it expands correctly. Then I want to collapse. prefix+/ and 'j' appears on that button, while I was expecting 'k'."

THE CAUSE: the letter IS the index. handle_hint_pick (heca/src/handlers.rs:799) enumerates targets in document order and calls candidate_letter(i) over a flat alphabet. Add or remove any target earlier in the tree and everything after it shifts by one. Expanding the pane changed the target list, and the button slid from k to j.

WHAT TO BUILD: remember the assignment across openings, keyed by the target's identity (T444). Two passes when the picker opens:
1. every target that had a letter last time and is still present keeps it;
2. the rest fill the gaps, in home-row-first order.
The memory lives as long as the session — a map on AppState beside offered_letters.

SIZE: small. A map plus a two-pass loop where the .enumerate() is now, roughly 40 lines.

⚠️ IT ONLY WORKS AS WELL AS THE IDENTITY DOES. Panes, rows, columns and docks are already named and become stable at once. An anonymous icon button is stable only once T444 gives it a derived identity — deriving from POSITION would not fix this bug at all, since expanding a pane is exactly what changes positions.

ORDER: do T443 (home row) FIRST. Changing the alphabet reshuffles everything once; doing it after this lands means learning the letters twice.

EDGE CASES
- A target that disappears must release its letter, or the pool leaks and later targets run out early (52 is the cap — section 2a, one letter always, never two).
- A remembered letter must not be handed to a different target while its owner is still on screen.
- Reopening the picker with an unchanged screen must give exactly the same letters — that is the test.

TEST: open, letter, change the tree elsewhere, reopen — a target present both times keeps its letter.

---
**Completion summary:**
DONE 2026-08-19 — verified against the description rather than assumed, after Antonio asked why it was still open. Shipped in 511715d (the two-pass assignment) and 8a540c8 (both pickers, stable button keys). Verified on screen by Antonio.

EVERY DELIVERABLE THIS TASK NAMED, AND WHERE IT IS
- the two-pass assignment: `assign_letters` (heca/src/handlers.rs:851) — pass 1 gives every present
  target the letter it had, pass 2 fills the gaps from DEFAULT_LETTERS in home-row-first order.
- the memory: `AppState::remembered_letters`, merged (not rebuilt) on each opening, so a target that
  is off screen keeps its letter for when it returns.
- THE TEST the task named — "reopening the picker with an unchanged screen must give exactly the
  same letters" → `reopening_an_unchanged_screen_gives_the_same_letters`.
- the original k→j report → `a_new_target_in_front_does_not_move_anyone_elses_letter`.
- edge "a departed target must release its letter or the pool leaks" →
  `a_departed_targets_letter_returns_to_the_pool`. NB the leak the task feared cannot happen anyway:
  the `taken` set holds only letters handed out *this* round, so a remembered entry for an absent
  target blocks nothing.
- edge "a remembered letter must not be handed to a different target while its owner is on screen" →
  `one_letter_never_goes_to_two_targets`.

WHAT MADE IT ACTUALLY WORK, beyond this task's own text
- It only works as well as the identity does, as the task warned. Panes were stable at once
  (`pane:7`), but the pane-HEADER buttons were not: they used the derived identity, which is computed
  from content, so zooming changed what the cluster rendered and their letters moved. Fixed in
  F011/P094/T451 with `.key(spec.action_name)` on the declaring wrapper — unique across panes without
  the pane id, because each header is its own hint surface (`pane-header:7/zoom`).
- prefix+q assigned by index until T451; all five pane pick modes now go through `assign_letters`, so
  the two pickers cannot drift apart.

WHY IT SAT OPEN: blocked on T447, which was folded into F011/P094/T451; nobody closed it afterwards.

tasks.title: Click-to-focus is two hit-tests in a tree that already gets the click — delete them for handlers
tasks.description:
**DONE 2026-08-25, commit `cb16a92`.** Closed on Antonio's instruction with verification PARTIAL — see the bottom of this note.

## What the user gets

Clicking anywhere in a sidebar focuses it, and clicking a row puts that container's cursor on the row you clicked, so the arrow keys carry on from there. Clicking the container's empty padding focuses it without moving the cursor. Right-click aims the keyboard identically, so the menu it opens describes the row the cursor is now on. None of that is new behaviour — it is the same behaviour, arrived at a different way.

## What changed underneath

Every mouse press used to run two geometric searches over the laid-out tree: which container contains this point, then which row sits under it. That is target-and-bubble re-implemented by measuring rectangles, in a tree that already receives the click as an event and already bubbles it. `Base::scope_key` existed only to make the first search findable, which is why it read as a strange property.

Now the container declares "a click in me focuses me" and the row declares "a click on me moves the cursor here". The row is reached first, the container after. A click on padding reaches only the container, so the padding rule falls out of the walk instead of being read off a second lookup. A plugin's panel gets both by writing the same one line.

## The new action

`WmAction::CursorTo { mount, key }` — the generic form of moving a mounted container's cursor, previously an internal function with a single caller. Full checklist: variant, `build_action` (not `action_from_name` — it needs a target), priority, handler, `build_registry`, catalog descriptor with both args declared required, `action_policy`, RPC verb `cursor-to`. **No default binding**, correctly: a key cannot supply a mount and a row key.

**First `WmAction` to carry `ActionPolicy::ContainerFocused`** — until now only name-keyed provider actions used it. Right family: it keeps "put the cursor on that row" out of the palette and RPC while nobody is driving a dock. A row emits `FocusDock` **before** `CursorTo`; events are queued and processed in order, so the domain is `Container` by the time the cursor moves. Same ordering a pane-header button uses when its action targets the focused pane.

## Deleted

`aim_keyboard_at_click` and both call sites, `chrome::container_at`, `chrome::key_at`, `nav::scope_at` and its two unit tests. Each was dead by the compiler's own reckoning before removal.

## Kept deliberately — do not "finish the job" by deleting it

**`Base::scope_key` survives.** `heca-grid-ui/src/hint/offer.rs:119` matches `key || scope_key`, and that `||` is how the **dock picker** lands a letter on a dock — a dock names itself with `scope_key`, not `key`. Deleting it silently breaks `prefix+Shift+e`. It now has that one reader and no hit-test. Retiring it means either giving the dock a `key` (which would make `collect_keys` return the dock itself as a steppable cursor row — the objection recorded in docs/widgets.md) or changing how the picker finds a dock. Its own task.

## A bug the suite caught, worth knowing

The click was first declared on the `KeyHint` wrapper around the row. `every_row_of_the_real_sidebar_tree_is_keyed_even_when_two_panes_share_a_name` failed: two panes named `zsh` became an ambiguous unkeyed collection. Making a **wrapper** activatable does it — the wrapper inherits the row's name through `text_summary` but carries no key. In user terms the app would have lost track of which of two identically-named panes the cursor, the right-click, the drag and the picker letter each meant. The declaration belongs on the row that carries the identity.

## ⚠️ VERIFICATION IS PARTIAL

Antonio confirmed **left click and right click work**. NOT confirmed on screen:
- clicking a dock's **empty padding** (should focus without moving the cursor),
- clicking inside a dock that **already** holds the keyboard (must not hand it back — `FocusDock` is idempotent since T444, but that is the case where a regression would show),
- **pressing the arrow keys after a click** (the cursor should continue from the row you clicked).

The last one is the whole point of the change. If any of these misbehave, this task is where to start.

tasks.title: The pane owns its letter — one picker mechanism, not two
tasks.description:
⭐ THE ONE ANTONIO IS WAITING ON. It blocks T445, and it is the root of two other reported bugs. Read the P082 handoff § 2(1) first — this is that finding written up.

THE REPORT (Antonio, driving, 2026-08-17): "i want to expand a pane, prefix+/ and `k` appears on that icon. I press k and it expands correctly. Then I want to collapse. prefix+/ and `j` appears on that button, while I was expecting `k`." T445 shipped a fix that does NOT cover this, because the letters he was looking at come from a different mechanism.

═══ THE DEFECT: TWO PICKERS, TWO MECHANISMS ═══

prefix+/  → handle_hint_pick → active_hint_targets → assign_letters (identity-based, stable)
          → each widget draws its own keycap through paint_child.

prefix+q  → handle_pane_select (heca/src/handlers.rs:781) → collect_all_pane_candidates(&session)
          → candidate_letter(INDEX). Those letters are drawn over panes by a HOST PAINT PASS at
            heca/src/app/render.rs:951 — a 48px glyph queued straight to state.text_renderer. No
            hint_label, no keycap, no key. Meanwhile its SIDEBAR letters come from
            offer_hint_by_key as proper keycaps.

One mode, two renderers, two looks, two assignment rules. render.rs already carries a comment saying no host pass may paint a keycap (from when paint_peek_letters was deleted); this one survived because it draws *pane candidates* rather than hint targets.

Because prefix+q assigns by index, anything that changes the candidate list or its order renumbers everything after it — which is the k→j report, and also why zoom and split shuffle the letters.

═══ ⚠️ ANTONIO'S RULE FOR THE FIX (2026-08-18) ═══
"terminal should not be responsible to render letters. They are programs that run inside pane. In the future there will be more apps inside pane. So pane is the container for every future app. If we are using terminal to render letters it is wrong."

So NEITHER app/render.rs NOR app/terminal_render.rs may own a pane's letter. The PANE CONTAINER declares its own identity and what picking it means; the framework draws the keycap. Then it works the same whatever runs inside — a terminal today, another app later.

And the general rule this is an instance of: WHOEVER OWNS THE THING DECLARES ITS IDENTITY; anything else displaying it is a view. A pane owns "pane:7". A sidebar row showing that pane is a second view of it, not the owner. Today that is inverted — the only declarer is a row inside the workspaces dock.

═══ ⚠️ AN ATTEMPT WAS MADE AND REVERTED — READ THIS BEFORE RETRYING ═══
Putting the declaration on the PANE HEADER and deleting the host pass broke prefix+q AND prefix+/ over panes. Two reasons, both still true:
1. heca/src/app/terminal_render.rs:800 paints the header with a DIRECT `header.root.paint(cx)` — not paint_child. Since T431 the framework draws a widget's letter inside paint_child, so nothing painted directly can ever show one.
2. The header is a thin strip at the top of the pane. The letter belongs CENTRED OVER THE PANE, which is where it is today and what Antonio expects (he sent a screenshot).
RESTORE FIRST IF YOU BREAK IT: `git checkout -- heca/src/app/render.rs heca/src/chrome/pane_header.rs`.

═══ WHAT TO BUILD ═══
1. A pane-level widget covering the pane declares `key(pane_key(id))` and what a pick does — focus that pane. Emitted through the seam the header buttons already use: `proxy.send_event(AppEvent::ChromeIntent { source, intent: InteractionIntent::FocusPane { pane_id } })`. The pane learns nothing about the sidebar, the picker or any other component (handoff § 3.7).
2. Whatever paints that widget must go through `heca_grid_ui::paint_child`, or the letter cannot draw. That includes fixing terminal_render.rs:800 if the header is involved.
3. Placement: centred over the pane. `HintPlacement::Center` on its hint style.
4. DELETE the host pass at app/render.rs:951 (~43 lines) — but only once 1–3 are proven on screen.
5. Then prefix+q assigns through `assign_letters` like prefix+/ does. That function (heca/src/handlers.rs) is pure and already written; it just needs the candidate list to carry identities.

═══ WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS ═══
- T445 stops being mis-scoped: one assignment rule for both pickers, so the k→j report is actually fixed.
- The letters stop being two different visual treatments for one gesture.
- prefix+q no longer depends on a component being mounted to show anything (handoff § 2(3)).

═══ VERIFICATION ═══
Rendering. Green tests prove nothing here. Antonio drives: prefix+q and prefix+/ with sidebars shown AND hidden, letters centred over panes, split a pane and check the others keep their letters, zoom in and out.

tasks.title: A pane's ancestors are positions, so splitting a column renames every pane after it
tasks.description:
Filed 2026-08-19. This was found during the 2026-08-18 hint work and written into the P082 handoff
§ 2(2), which left it explicitly undecided — "decide whether that is T444 or its own task". Nobody
decided, so it had NO task while remaining live. It is not part of T444 (that is now the enforcement)
and not part of T446 (that is scope_key).

═══ THE DEFECT ═══
A pane's own identity is stable — `pane_key(id)` is a real `PaneId` and survives every rebuild. Its
ANCESTORS are not:

    pane_key(pane)              → "pane:7"      ← stable, a real PaneId
    workspace_key(ws_idx)       → "ws:0"        ← an INDEX
    column_key(ws_idx, col_idx) → "col:0:2"     ← TWO indices

(all in heca/src/providers/workspaces/mod.rs, beside the comment that says positions must never
appear in a key that has an id available — which is exactly what these do.)

A sidebar pane row's full identity is therefore `chrome/ws:0/col:0:2/pane:7`. **Splitting inserts a
column**, so every column after it renumbers and every pane inside changes identity — even though
none of those panes moved and none of them changed. Anything keyed on that identity resets: the hint
letter (F003/P082/T445), and the cursor, right-click target and drag identity that read the same
string.

The pane's OWN tree is unaffected (F011/P094/T451 gave it `pane:7` with no positional ancestors), so
today the two views of one pane disagree: the pane keeps its letter across a split, its sidebar row
does not. That asymmetry is the visible symptom.

═══ WHAT TO BUILD ═══
`Column::id: ColumnId` and `Workspace::id: WorkspaceId` BOTH ALREADY EXIST in heca-core. The work is
threading them through instead of the enumerated positions:
- `workspace_key` / `column_key` take ids, not indices.
- The candidate lists carry them: `collect_workspace_candidates` /`collect_column_candidates`
  (heca/src/app/selection.rs) yield `ws_idx`/`col_idx` today.
- The providers build rows from `enumerate()` positions (heca/src/providers/workspaces/) — they need
  the id from the model instead.
- `move_provider_cursor` matches on the resulting string, so it moves with them.

⚠️ IT CANNOT BE DONE HALFWAY. The cursor, the right-click target and drag all read these keys; a
partial change leaves two spellings of one row and something silently pointing at the wrong one.

═══ VERIFICATION ═══
Antonio drives. Open `prefix+/`, note a pane row's letter in the sidebar, SPLIT a column to its left,
reopen — the row must keep its letter, exactly as the pane itself now does. Same for the keyboard
cursor and a right-click after a split.
