    Overlay::new().panel(body).animation(Fade::new())
    Overlay::new().panel(body).animation(ZoomFade::new().from(0.8))
    Overlay::new().panel(body).animation(MyPluginSlide::new())   // <- their own, no host change

One builder on the widget. No id, no registry, no host-private type, and NO enum a plugin cannot
extend. A third-party animation must be possible **without touching heca-grid-ui** — that is the
difference between a trait and an enum, and it is why Antonio asked for a trait.

═══ WHY THIS IS A BUG, NOT A FEATURE REQUEST ═══
The capability is trapped in `LayerRegistry` (`heca/src/chrome/layers.rs`), which is `pub(crate)`.
To get what the exposé has, an author writes three calls on a registry while holding an id:

    let id = state.layers.add(parent, kind, modal, covers, root);
    state.layers.set_fade_out_after(id, FADE_OUT, ZOOM_IN * FADE_LAG);
    state.layers.set_zoom(id, ZOOM_IN, from);

…and must know the sequencing rule themselves (the lag is a SHARE of the zoom, never a second
absolute duration). A plugin can reach none of it. Exactly the shape ⭐⭐ RULE ZERO forbids — the
same defect `HintTargetRegistry` had before F004/P084/T399 deleted it.

`Overlay` (heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/overlay.rs) has NO animation at all. Verified 2026-08-20: its
whole builder surface is `panel` :584, `panel_boxed` :595, `panel_size` :625, `blocking` :655,
`position` :662, `anchored` :672, `open` :718, `open_signal` :724, `on_outside_click` :732,
`panel_bounds` :738. Opening is a bool with no transition.

═══ 1. THE `Animation` TRAIT (heca-grid-ui) ═══
An animation is a thing that, given progress through an arrival or an exit, says how the surface
should be drawn. It owns its own timing and reports when it is finished:

    pub trait Animation {
        fn tick(&mut self, dt: f32) -> bool;   // true while moving; mirrors Component::tick
        fn enter(&mut self);
        fn leave(&mut self);
        fn cancel(&mut self);
        fn is_leaving(&self) -> bool;          // still playing an EXIT — see Exit below
        fn frame(&self) -> AnimationFrame;     // { opacity, scale, offset }
    }

`AnimationFrame` is the whole vocabulary a surface's presentation needs, so a new animation adds no
new plumbing: a slide sets `offset`, a fade sets `opacity`, a zoom sets `scale`, and the painter
applies all three where it already applies opacity and `PaintCx::with_scale`. **Adding an animation
must not require a change in the painter** — that is the test for whether the vocabulary is right.
If a future one needs something outside it (a rotation, a clip), add it to the frame ONCE, centrally.

Ship: `Fade`, `Zoom` (with `from`), their **composition** (the dissolve RIDES the movement, lagging
by a SHARE of it — never a second duration that can drift), and `NoAnimation` (the default: a cut,
so a surface that declares nothing costs nothing and needs no special case).

`heca-grid-ui/src/effects.rs` already has `Fade` (with `delay`) and `Zoom` (`enter`/`leave`/
`cancel`/`is_leaving`/`amount`), both correct and tested; `Zoom::amount` rests at `from` after a
leave (F003/P082/T327). **Build ON these — do not rewrite them.** They have exactly ONE consumer in
the repo today (`LayerRegistry`), so nothing is duplicated yet; this task stops that becoming N
consumers each re-deriving the rules.

═══ 2. `Exit` — THE COMPOSITION BECOMES A TYPE ═══
Today `DynamicLayer::is_leaving()` composes `fade.is_running() || zoom.is_leaving()` app-side. "A
surface's exit is one gesture made of several effects, and it is not over until every one has
finished" is a general truth about effects, not about layers — a plugin building its own animated
surface would have to rediscover it. Getting it wrong made `Fade::delay` unusable for a week: a
layer was retired when its FADE ended, so the cards stayed on screen after the map had gone
(F003/P082/T327). With the trait, `is_leaving` is one method and a composite answers for all its
parts — a type guarantee rather than something the host knows.

═══ 3. `Overlay` DELEGATES — it does not implement animation ═══
    Overlay::new().panel(body).animation(impl Animation + 'static)

`Overlay` owns appearing/disappearing as a CONCEPT and hands the how to the `Animation`. It already
owns the scrim, the panel chrome, the placement and `open`; the animation joins that list. `open`
becomes "begin arriving / begin leaving" rather than an instant bool — and a surface with
`NoAnimation` behaves exactly as today. The painter applies `AnimationFrame` in ONE place, so no
widget and no host re-implements it.

═══ 4. THE DECLARATIVE HALF — one door, never two ═══
A described node names its animation, so a plugin sending JSON gets identical behaviour to native
code. Names resolve the way a **theme colour token** does (docs/widgets.md → "Appearance: the theme
is the default, not a wall"): unknown name ⇒ the default, debug-logged, never a panic — `realize`
stays total for untrusted input.

═══ 5. THE EXPOSÉ BECOMES AN OVERLAY — Antonio's explicit requirement ═══
"The expose must be an instance of the Overlay or a child and reuse all the Overlay API for
animation, appearing etc."

Today `heca/src/chrome/expose/mod.rs` is a bespoke layer: it builds its own root and drives fade,
zoom and backdrop through three `LayerRegistry` calls, with `FADE_OUT` / `ZOOM_IN` / `FADE_LAG` as
private constants. After this task it declares an `Overlay` with an `Animation`, exactly as a plugin
would — which is the proof the API is real. **If the exposé still needs anything the `Overlay` API
cannot express, THAT is the missing builder: add it to `Overlay`, never special-case the exposé.**
`set_fade_out_after` / `set_zoom` then stop being public surface on `LayerRegistry`.

═══ 6. FILE STRUCTURE — one file, one thing, exactly as § 0b-bis lays it out ═══
Antonio, 2026-08-20: "animation and expose must follow the code structure described in AGENTS.md
chrome/expose, and for effects maybe animation/fade.rs, animation/bounce.rs etc… and for example an
animation/mod.rs for common things if needed."

    heca-grid-ui/src/animation/
    ├── mod.rs        the `Animation` TRAIT, `AnimationFrame`, shared easing, re-exports
    ├── fade.rs       Fade
    ├── zoom.rs       Zoom
    ├── sequence.rs   the composition — one animation riding another, lag as a SHARE
    ├── none.rs       NoAnimation (the default)
    └── bounce.rs     … and every future one is a NEW FILE, nothing else edited

That last line is the point of the whole task. Adding `bounce.rs` must touch **no other file** — no
enum arm, no painter match, no registry. If it does, the trait or `AnimationFrame` is wrong; fix the
model, not the new file.

`mod.rs` holds only what is genuinely common — the trait, the frame, easing shared by several
animations. Not a dumping ground: an animation's own timing belongs to that animation.

**What moves, what stays.** `effects.rs` holds `Flash` :8, `Attention` :63, `Eased` :133, `Fade`
:201, `Zoom` :394. `Fade` and `Zoom` are *surface* animations and move into `animation/`; `Flash`,
`Attention` and `Eased` are per-widget effects (a press flash, an attention pulse, a smoothed value)
with different consumers, and stay. Re-export `Eased` from `animation/mod.rs` if the animations need
it — reuse it, never write a second easing.

**The app side already follows § 0b-bis** (`heca/src/chrome/expose/`: `mod.rs` host wiring — the
only file that may touch `AppState` — plus `model.rs`, `pane_card.rs`, `column_card.rs`,
`workspace_row.rs`, `expose_grid.rs`, `testing.rs`). Keep that shape. Becoming an `Overlay` changes
`mod.rs`, which is where host wiring belongs, and must not push presentation into the component
files or geometry into `mod.rs`.

**Sizes stay shares.** § 0b: a composition that multiplies model numbers by a scale of its own has
taken over the layout engine's job. An animation's `scale` is a PAINT transform
(`PaintCx::with_scale`), never a layout number — animating a surface must not reintroduce computed
pixels into the exposé, which took seven attempts to remove.

═══ WHAT MUST SURVIVE — every one found by DRIVING, none by tests ═══
- A finished LEAVE rests at `from`, not back at life size (else the cards flash to full size as they
  fade — F003/P082/T327).
- Re-showing a surface that is LEAVING must not cancel its exit. The exposé hits this on the
  ordinary path: it dismisses itself and THEN focuses the pane you chose, and focusing rebuilds the
  map mid-exit.
- The tick that ENDS an exit must still request a frame, to paint the absence — otherwise the last
  frame drawn still shows the surface faintly until some other input forces a repaint.
- A dissolving surface holds no input (`is_active`), and removal waits for the WHOLE exit.
- `add_named`'s in-place replacement keeps a layer's place, its visibility AND its animation in
  flight (a rebuild must not replay an arrival).

═══ VERIFICATION ═══
Animation is visible behaviour: Antonio drives it. Green tests found NONE of the three exit bugs —
all three came from tracing the running frame (per-layer `op`/`scale`, per frame) after three
diagnoses by inspection were each wrong. Instrument before concluding.

═══ THE STANDING RULE THIS TASK EXISTS TO HONOUR ═══
Antonio, repeatedly, 2026-08-19/20: "don't make fix hardcoding code around. they should be
centralized. Don't let me repeat this other 100000 times" · "Please, as always, try to centralize
resolutions. do not just fix the call" · "always think of extensibility, plugin authors, and
reusability". Before writing a fix at a call site, ask whether a second author would hit the same
thing — if yes, it belongs in the model.

---

One file per member: mod.rs (trait, `AnimationFrame{opacity,scale,offset}`, `smoothstep`, `AnimationFrame::apply` — the one place a frame becomes a picture), fade.rs, zoom.rs, sequence.rs (lag = a SHARE of the lead), zoom_fade.rs (the exposé's gesture, defined ONCE), vocabulary.rs, presence.rs.

tasks.title: The column in the scrolling area does not own its identity — only its sidebar view does
tasks.description:
Found by Antonio driving T438, 2026-08-24: "prefix+shift+c works but show letters only in the sidebar. not in the scrolling area. not sure this is what we deciced." It is not. It is the ownership inversion already decided against, still open for columns.

⚠️ TWO PARTS. (A) the identity fix below, and (B) a new action Antonio asked for on 2026-08-24 — move the current pane to a NEW column. They ship together because they are the same gesture: when the column pick is up you are choosing a destination, and "a column that does not exist yet" is one of the destinations.

═══════════ PART A — the column owns its identity ═══════════

THE RULE, ALREADY SETTLED
P082(F003)/T447: "WHOEVER OWNS THE THING DECLARES ITS IDENTITY; anything else displaying it is a view. A pane owns 'pane:7'. A sidebar row showing that pane is a second view of it, not the owner. Today that is inverted — the only declarer is a row inside the workspaces dock."

That was fixed FOR PANES by P094(F011)/T451 (done, verified on screen): the pane shell carries `.key(pane_key(id))`, `pane_key` was given ONE home in heca/src/chrome/mod.rs, and the sidebar row became a view of it. Columns never got the same treatment.

WHAT HAPPENS
`prefix+Ctrl+c` (`move_pane_to_column_pick` — rebound from prefix+Shift+c by T476) letters every column, and the letters appear ONLY on the sidebar's column groups. The columns you are looking at, in the scrolling area, get nothing — so the pick asks you to aim at a target visible only in a dock you may have collapsed.

WHY — traced, not guessed
Letters are offered BY KEY: heca/src/chrome/hint/letters.rs:80 makes `Offer::ByKey(column_key(ws, col))`, and `offer_hint_by_key` lands it on whatever widget carries that key. The only widget carrying it is the SIDEBAR's — heca/src/providers/workspaces/column_group.rs:71:

    MarkerGroup::new().key(column_key(ws_idx, column.col_idx))

Nothing in the scrolling area declares it, so the letter has nowhere to go. It is not dropped by candidacy and not clipped — there is no target.

The handler's doc comment (heca/src/handlers.rs:995) says "shown as a `KeyHint` over its **sidebar** column", i.e. written to the pre-T447 model. That comment is wrong now and goes with the fix.

WHAT TO BUILD
The same shape as T451, one level up: the thing that OWNS a column declares `column_key(..)` and what picking it means; the sidebar's `MarkerGroup` keeps showing the letter as a VIEW, exactly as the sidebar pane row does for a pane. Do not add a second lettering path for the content area — ⭐⭐ RULE ZERO and the DRY rule both forbid it, and T451 already proved the by-key offer reaches every view of one identity.

Answer BEFORE writing code, by tracing:
- **Is there a column-level component in the scrolling area at all?** T451 had to BUILD `heca/src/chrome/pane/` because no pane component existed. If columns are the same, this task is "the column becomes a component", not "add a key". Check before scoping.
- **Where does `column_key` live?** It is in heca/src/providers/workspaces/mod.rs today; if chrome/ needs it, it MOVES rather than being copied — that is what T451 had to do for `pane_key`.

═══════════ PART B — move the current pane to a NEW column ═══════════
Antonio, 2026-08-24: "A new action to move the current pane to a new column."

PRE-FLIGHT — it does not exist. Checked:
- `SplitHorizontal` ("split_horizontal", prefix+Enter) — creates a NEW PANE in a new column. Does not move the pane you are on.
- `MovePaneToColumn { col_idx }` (input.rs:197) — stacks the active pane into an EXISTING column.
- `move_pane_left` / `move_pane_right` (prefix+Ctrl+[ / ]) — walk between EXISTING columns.
Nothing extracts the current pane into a column of its own. The nearest neighbours are `SplitHorizontal` for "make a column here" and `MovePaneToColumn` for "put this pane in that column"; the new action is their intersection and should read like both.

WHAT TO BUILD — the full § "Adding New Actions" checklist, all 11 steps, not a shortcut:
1. A `WmAction` variant in heca/src/input.rs.
2. `action_from_name()` — the bare name says everything (it acts on the focused pane and needs no
   target), so it belongs there, unlike the *_pick actions.
3. `action_priority()` — explicit arm, no catch-all.
4. Handler in heca/src/handlers.rs. It must NOT compute geometry: the column insert lives in
   heca-core/src/layout, the same way every other structural action does.
5. `build_registry()` in heca/src/app/registry.rs.
6. A default binding in keybindings.default.toml — an action with no default is the exact bug T476
   just fixed. Pick it beside the neighbours it reads like (the split and move-pane families).
7. Descriptor in `ActionRegistry::ALL` with declared `args` (`args: &[]` if it takes none — the
   field has no default, so the question cannot be skipped).
8. `action_policy()` in heca/src/app/interaction.rs — the match is exhaustive so it will not compile
   until classified. It restructures the tiled layout, so `TiledOnly` is the likely arm; confirm
   against the table rather than assuming.
9. RPC parser support in heca/src/rpc.rs.
10. README.md key table + keybindings.default.toml comment.
11. Reachable from mouse/UI, keyboard and RPC — not trapped behind one surface.

Settle with Antonio:
- **Where does the new column go** — immediately right of the current one (like split_horizontal),
  or at the end of the strip?
- **Does it appear as a target in the `prefix+Ctrl+c` pick** — a "new column" letter alongside the
  existing ones? That is the reason A and B are one task. If yes, it needs somewhere to draw that
  letter, which Part A is what makes possible.
- **What happens to a pane that is alone in its column** — the move is a no-op, or refused with the
  feedback P082(F003)/T475 is about?

═══════════ ORDER — READ THIS ═══════════
⚠️ **P082(F003)/T458 changes what `column_key` IS.** It replaces the positional `column_key(ws_idx, col_idx)` → "col:0:2" with one built from the `ColumnId` that already exists in heca-core, because a split renumbers every column after it and resets everything keyed on the old spelling. Declaring the positional key in a second place first means threading the id change through two declarers instead of one. Settle with Antonio whether T458 lands first, or the two are done together.

═══════════ VERIFICATION ═══════════
Rendering. Green tests do not show where a letter is, and every defect in T451 was found by eye against a green suite. Antonio drives:
- `prefix+Ctrl+c` with two or more columns letters the scrolling area AND the sidebar; the typed letter moves the active pane into that column; the letters withdraw together; check with the sidebar shown and hidden.
- Watch for the same-letter-drawn-twice question — correct if the two are one target seen in two places (as a pane and its sidebar row already are), but confirm by eye and check the identity rule does not warn about a duplicate key.
- Part B: the new action moves the focused pane out into its own column, the strip re-lays out, and the pane keeps its letter across the move (which is what T458 is about — if it does not, that is T458 and not a regression here).

tasks.title: A pick with no candidates dies silently — the key looks broken
tasks.description:
Found by Antonio driving T438, 2026-08-24: "prefix+g do nothing. what should it be?" — with one workspace open. With two, it letters correctly, so the pick itself is sound.

WHAT HAPPENS
`prefix+g` is `move_pane_to_workspace_pick`. `collect_workspace_candidates` (`heca/src/app/selection.rs:73`) filters out the ACTIVE workspace — correct, you cannot move a pane where it already is. With a single workspace open that leaves an empty list, and `handle_move_pane_to_workspace_pick` (`heca/src/handlers.rs:979`) returns without entering the mode:

    let Some(pane_id) = state.focused_pane else { return; };
    let candidates = collect_workspace_candidates(&state.session);
    if !candidates.is_empty() { … }        // ← nothing at all happens if it is empty

No prompt, no message, no flash. The key is indistinguishable from unbound, which is exactly how a user concludes a feature is broken.

THIS IS NOT ONE HANDLER'S BUG
Every pick handler has the same two silent exits — no focused pane, or no candidates:
- `handle_move_column_to_workspace_pick` (handlers.rs:960)
- `handle_move_pane_to_workspace_pick` (handlers.rs:979)
- `handle_move_pane_to_column_pick` (handlers.rs:997)
and the pane/swap/take picks have the same shape. Per the no-per-widget-copies rule, fixing one handler is the wrong move: N copies of a rule means the rule belongs one level up.

WHERE IT SHOULD LIVE
The pick modes already share a vocabulary — `InputMode::pending_pick()` (`heca/src/app_state.rs:252`) maps each mode to its action and pulls the human prompt and label from the `ActionCatalog`, which is the single source of truth for action text. A refused pick should report through that same seam, so a plugin's pick gets the feedback heca's does with nothing written. Reach for the existing notification path (`ToastSpec` / the toast stack) rather than inventing a per-pick message channel.

Decide with Antonio before building:
- What a refused pick should DO — a toast, the existing prompt bar showing "no other workspace", or a brief flash on the thing that would have been the target. Do not guess; this is the visible half.
- Whether "no focused pane" and "no candidates" read the same to the user, or want different words.

VERIFY
With exactly one workspace: `prefix+g` says something instead of nothing. With two or more it letters as it does today — Antonio confirmed that path already works, so the fix must not disturb it. He drives the check.

Antonio, 2026-08-24: "we need to provide a default binding always. I'd suggest prefix+shift+c = rename column, prefix+ctrl+c [the pick]." Confirmed he means the action bound to prefix+Shift+c today, `move_pane_to_column_pick`, moved as-is — not a new "peek" action.

THE DEFECT

tasks.title: A sidebar pane row that had no cwd when it was built can never show one
tasks.description:
Found by Antonio driving T438, 2026-08-24 (screenshot): some sidebar pane rows show the folder icon + `~` path line, others show only `zsh` with nothing under it. Adjacent rows in the same column, same program.

WHERE
heca/src/providers/workspaces/pane_row.rs:224-259.

    let cwd_path = runtime.as_ref().and_then(|rt| rt.cwd.clone());
    let cwd_text  = cwd_path.as_deref().map(home_relative_path);
    let cwd = crate::components::FolderLine { path: cwd_text.as_deref(), show: ws_state.pane_show_cwd(), .. };
    let show_cwd = ws_state.pane_show_cwd() && cwd_text.is_some();
    ...
    if show_cwd {                      // ← the row is only ATTACHED when this is true at BUILD time
        column = column.child(Flex::row()...child(cwd_row));
    }

HYPOTHESIS — not yet proved, instrument before changing anything
The file's own comment two lines above says the opposite of what the code does: "the row's visibility follows `[settings] pane_show_cwd` and whether the pane has a cwd … a `cd` updates the path in place, and `pane_show_cwd` turns the line on and off the same way." The `FolderLine` does carry a `visible` signal for exactly that.

But the row is only added as a CHILD when `show_cwd` is true at build time. A pane whose runtime has no `cwd` yet is built without the row at all, and no signal can reveal a child that is not in the tree. It would then take a rebuild to appear — and if the rebuild key does not include the cwd, that rebuild never comes.

That matches the symptom exactly: whether a row has its path line depends on whether the cwd had arrived at the instant that row was built, which is why it looks arbitrary and differs between neighbours.

INSTRUMENT FIRST (the rule that has paid off every time here — six wrong guesses in one day on the exposé, one round of tracing named it)
Log, per pane, at build: `pane_id`, `runtime.is_some()`, `rt.cwd`, `show_cwd`, and whether the child was attached. Then watch a pane that is missing its line — does its `cwd` become `Some` later while `show_cwd` stayed false? That confirms it in one round. Do NOT change the attach condition before seeing this.

IF CONFIRMED, THE FIX SHAPE
Attach the row ALWAYS and let its `visible` signal decide — which is what the comment already describes and what `Visibility` is for. Then a cwd arriving later flips a signal instead of needing a rebuild, and `pane_show_cwd` keeps working the same way. Check the empty row costs no vertical space when hidden (`Visibility` folds it out of layout, but confirm on screen — an empty gap under half the rows is a worse bug than the one being fixed).

VERIFY
Antonio drives. Open panes, `cd` in one of them, and watch the line appear without the row being rebuilt. Check a freshly spawned pane gets its line as soon as the cwd is known, and that toggling `[settings] pane_show_cwd` still turns every line on and off.

tasks.title: A zero-width pane still gets a letter, drawn outside itself in the gutter
tasks.description:
Found by tracing T438 case 4 (narrow window), 2026-08-24. This is the explanation of the letter pile-up Antonio photographed, and it is NOT the clamp that was first suspected.

MEASURED, not reasoned. Temporary probe at heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/key_hint.rs (paint_hint_label), printing placement / row bounds / clip / room / cap / fitted for every letter. 9060 lines over one session. The probe has been removed.

THE DATA
    [hint] "p" place=Center row=(318,40 0x728) clip=none room=EMPTY cap=(308,394) -> (308,394)
    [hint] "v" place=Center row=(314,40 0x728) clip=none room=EMPTY cap=(304,394) -> (304,394)

Read the row size: **0x728**. Two panes with ZERO WIDTH, each still handed a letter.

`HintPlacement::Center` computes `x = loc.x + (w - capW) / 2`. With `w = 0` that is `loc.x - capW/2` — the cap is centred on a pane that has no width, so it lands OUTSIDE the pane, half a keycap to its left. At 318 and 314 the two caps are 4px apart and overlap each other.

THAT IS THE PILE-UP. In the first screenshot several letters sat side by side in the narrow gutter between the two sidebars, looking like they had been dragged there. They had not been dragged anywhere: they are zero-width panes' own Center caps, drawn where the arithmetic puts them, stacking on each other because the panes they belong to are all at nearly the same x.

WHY THE PANES ARE ZERO-WIDTH: two sidebars, each 288 logical px (clip=(6,50 288x708) and (306,50 288x708)), in a window ~575 wide. The sidebars consume the whole width and the scrolling area is squeezed to nothing.

THE DEFECT IS CANDIDACY, NOT PLACEMENT
A pane you cannot see is not a target — you cannot aim at it, and activating it by letter is a gesture with no visible referent. `heca_grid_ui::hint::collect` already drops a target outside its clipping ancestors; it does not drop one that has collapsed to zero (or near-zero) size. A pane at 0x728 passes every existing check because it is technically inside its clip.

FIX SHAPE — one rule, in the collector, not per widget
Drop a candidate whose laid-out bounds cannot hold its own cap. That is the same judgement `fit_into_view` already makes at the other end ("None when the visible sliver is too small to hold the cap"), applied one level up where it decides whether to spend a letter at all. Doing it in the collector also means the letter is not wasted — there are only 52.

⚠️ Do NOT fix this by clamping the Center placement into the pane's bounds. A zero-width pane has no inside; clamping would stack every cap on one pixel instead of four, which is the same bug with a smaller radius.

Decide with Antonio: is the threshold "smaller than its own keycap", or something more generous (a pane you can see a sliver of is arguably still aimable, which is the rule for a half-visible sidebar row)? The two cases differ — a sidebar row's letter is drawn INSIDE the row, a pane's is centred, so a sliver of pane cannot hold a centred cap the way a sliver of row can.

RELATED, SAME TRACE, SEPARATE TASKS
- 474 compact `TopCenter` caps were yanked back onto the icons they caption — filed separately.
- The two sidebars overflow the window at this width (the right one's clip runs to x=594 in a ~575-wide window, which is why the workspace dock's "d" keycap is cut in half by the window edge). That is a layout problem, not a hint one.

VERIFY
Antonio drives. Narrow the window until the scrolling area is squeezed away, press prefix+/ — no letters in the gutter, and no letter spent on a pane nobody can see. Widen it again and the pane's letter comes back, centred over the pane.

tasks.title: A compact target's caption is dragged back on top of the icon it captions
tasks.description:
Found by tracing T438, 2026-08-24. Two rules that are each correct, and compose into a wrong one. 474 occurrences in a single session, every one a compact target.

MEASURED, not reasoned. Temporary probe in heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/key_hint.rs (paint_hint_label) printing placement / row / clip / room / cap / fitted. Probe removed after the trace.

THE DATA
    [hint] "w" place=TopCenter row=(526,48 26x25) clip=(316,40 320x728)
                                room=(526,48 26x25) cap=(531,75) -> (531,56)

The cap is placed at y=75 and moved to y=56. Of 474 caps the clamp moved in that session, **all 474 were `TopCenter`**, and **none** was moved horizontally — the narrow-window horizontal-overflow theory was wrong and is disproved by this data.

THE CONTRADICTION
`keycap_rect` (key_hint.rs:427) puts a compact target's cap deliberately OUTSIDE the target:
"A target too small to cover goes beside it, not over it. Centred just below, so the icon stays fully visible with its letter as a caption."
For a 25px-tall button at y=48 that is `48 + 25 + HINT_ADJACENT_GAP` = y=75.

`fit_into_view` (key_hint.rs:498) then clamps the cap into `bounds ∩ clip` — and `bounds` is that same 25px button. y=75 is outside it, so the cap is dragged back to ~56: **on top of the icon it was supposed to caption**. The beside-placement is undone by the line immediately after it.

Both rules are individually right and individually documented, in the same file, a few lines apart. `fit_into_view` is correct for a `CenterRight` cap drawn INSIDE its row — the case it was written for ("a row half past a sidebar's fold keeps its letter … moved inside the visible part of its own row"). It is wrong for a cap whose placement deliberately puts it outside its target.

It fires for every compact target that has a clipping ancestor, at ANY window width. Nothing tested it, so nothing failed.

FIX SHAPE
`fit_into_view` needs to know which rect the cap is allowed to live in, and that is not always `bounds`. For a compact target the permitted area is the target PLUS its caption band (above and below), intersected with the clip; for every other placement it stays `bounds ∩ clip`. Compute that permitted rect where the placement is decided — `keycap_rect` already knows which branch it took — and hand it to `fit_into_view` instead of re-deriving the answer from `bounds` alone.

⚠️ Do not special-case `is_compact` inside `fit_into_view` by calling it a second time. Two places asking the same question is how the two rules drifted apart in the first place; the branch that CHOSE the placement is the one that knows.

TESTS
key_hint.rs's own test module already covers the row cases (`an_unclipped_cap_is_left_where_it_was_placed`, the sliver case). Add the missing one: a compact target with a clipping ancestor keeps its cap BELOW itself, and flips above only when below would leave the viewport. That test is what would have caught this.

VERIFY
Antonio drives. `prefix+/` with the top bar visible: every icon button's letter sits below (or above, near the bottom edge) the icon, never on it. Check inside a pane header too, since that was the case that produced the earlier wrong-viewport bug.

tasks.title: A sidebar pane's name is built twice and stacked, so it and the program name never share a line
tasks.description:
**DONE 2026-08-25**, verified on screen by Antonio. Five commits: `c4352ac` `33a702f` `c685769` `aaf8c55` `310e697`.

## What the user gets

A renamed pane's name and its dimmed `(program)` suffix sit on one line, on one baseline, and neither moves when the pane is selected or deselected.

## Three layers, only the top one visible

The reported symptom was the name jumping across the suffix as selection changed. Underneath were three separate defects, each the cause of the one above it:

1. **The row built the name twice** — one copy coloured for selected, one for not — stacked them vertically and hid whichever did not apply. The hidden copy kept its slot, so the visible name sat at the top of the stack when selected and the bottom when not.
2. **The selectable row did not publish its state colour**, which is *why* the name had to exist twice. `Item` had always published one; `Row` had not, so any caller wanting text that follows selection had to colour it themselves — and a colour is fixed at build time, so "follows selection" could only be done by building the content twice.
3. **Two runs of text at different sizes could not share a line at all.** The renderer centres each run's line box in its rect and drops the baseline an ascent below; both scale with font size, so centring the boxes leaves the smaller run's baseline above the larger one's. Start aligns tops, End aligns bottoms — none of the four alignments means "on one line".

## What was built

- `Row` publishes its state colour, as `Item` always did. One name now, carrying no colour of its own.
- **`Flex` gives a row of text runs one shared baseline** — it measures where each run's baseline falls inside its own box and drops the shallower ones until they meet the deepest. The row never grows; a run only moves into space a taller sibling already claimed.
- `PaneName`'s colour became `Option`: unset means inherit. The exposé card, which owns its colour, still passes one.
- Four live values tracking the name collapsed to one.
- The gap between the two runs comes from the font-relative spacing token instead of a hardcoded 4px.

## Three wrong turns, recorded so they are not repeated

- **A call-site workaround.** With no baseline support, both runs were forced to the same font size — which works, and is a design decision made to paper over a layout defect. Antonio: *"Fix it centralized not in the site call. We need to have all Flex widget have this fix."* Reverted.
- **A vocabulary word that lied.** `Align::Baseline` was added, found to produce byte-identical output to `Align::End` (the engine takes a baseline from a container's first child; a text leaf measures itself and reports none), and then **documented as broken and kept**. Antonio: *"you want to pollute the code. IF it work keep otherwise fix or remove."* **Removed.** Do not re-add it: baseline alignment of text is the row container's job, not an alignment option's.
- **Proving it on a shape that does not occur.** The baseline pass was declared working against a probe of two bare labels. The real row wraps its suffix in a visibility toggle, the pass asked each direct child "are you text?", the wrapper said no and was skipped — so the misalignment survived while the test reported success. The pass now looks **through** transparent wrappers to the text inside, which is what transparent means. **Test the shape that actually occurs.**

## One judgement reversed by the user

The suffix was dimmed to `muted` on request, and it is unreadable against the selected row's fill. The line it replaced said so — *"`foreground` (not `muted`) so it's readable on every theme"* — and the reason was dropped with it. Back to `foreground`; it reads as secondary through its smaller size and the parentheses, neither of which costs legibility.

## Held by tests

Three in `Flex`: runs of different sizes share a baseline; **a wrapped run joins them** (the case that was missed); and aligning never makes the row taller.

tasks.title: A leading icon or handle is placed without consulting the row's width, so content escapes the box
tasks.description:
A leading icon or handle is placed without consulting the row's width, so content escapes the box.

Carried out of the P082 handoff, where it was recorded as the open remainder of T438 but never had a task of its own. T438 closed on the sidebar letter positions; this did not close with it.

THE DEFECT — "class 3"
Some kinds put a leading icon or a drag handle before their text WITHOUT consulting the row's width. The text is then laid out from wherever the leading element ended, so at a narrow width the content is pushed past the box's own edge. `DockFrame` at 60px puts its title **entirely outside** its box. Affected kinds as recorded: `ItemGroup`, `DockFrame`, `Toast`, `Item`.

═══ WHAT WAS BUILT (2026-08-25, branch `feat/hint-anything-actionable`, UNCOMMITTED) ═══

**1. Three of the four were ONE framework defect, fixed in the layout pass — no widget touched.**
`heca-grid-ui/src/layout.rs`, beside T438's `max_width: Pct(1.0)` cap: a child of a non-viewport parent now gets `min_width: Px(0.0)` unless it set one. Flexbox's `min-width: auto` floors every item at its own content width, so a row whose children were *willing* to shrink still could not fit them and laid the overflow out past its own edge. `ItemGroup`, `DockFrame` (both widths) and `Item` were fixed by that one rule. Opt-out is unchanged: an explicit `min_width` or `shrink(0.0)` is left alone. Not applied inside a viewport (`clips_children`) — there the floor is what keeps a 600px column 600px wide in a 100px scroll region. Two tests in `layout.rs`: a leading slot never pushes the text past the row's edge, and a widget that refuses to shrink keeps its size.

**2. The catalog sweep's five escapes were PHANTOM — a defect in the sweeps themselves.**
Both sweeps walked the clip stack with `clips.last().and_then(|c| c.intersection(r)).unwrap_or(*r)`: a clip lying **entirely outside** the clip already open has an empty intersection, and `unwrap_or` read that as "no clip in force", reporting every draw inside it at its raw position. All five were draws inside a widget laid out past the showcase page's scroll viewport — fully scissored, never on screen. Two copies of that arithmetic, both wrong the same way.
Fixed as ONE implementation: `Scene::draws_outside(within) -> Vec<Escape>` (`heca-grid-ui/src/scene.rs`), base layer only, empty clip = nothing drawn. Both sweeps now call it; ~40 lines of duplicated walking deleted from each. Three tests in `scene.rs`.

**3. `Toast` was composed (Antonio's call, asked 2026-08-25).**
It measured its own icon, title, body, action and × in pixels, drew them, and decided what the pointer was over by testing coordinates against those rects — so no framework rule could reach it. Now: leading `Icon`, a text column (title / body / action), and the × are real children the engine lays out. `rects()`, `region_at()` and the `Rects` struct are gone; the card paints only its chrome — tinted surface, bracket frame, the action's face at the rect the ENGINE gave it, the press flash, the focus ring. The action and the × take their own press through `on_pointer_down` handlers and stop propagation; the card's `on_click` moved from capture to bubble and fires for what its children declined. Height is now the engine's answer (it hugs), not a formula.
Severity tone is **published** via `with_content_color`, so the icon and title inherit it — the mechanism `Item` already uses.

**4. `ToastStack` had the same shape and had to follow.**
It read a height the card pinned on itself and wrote a rect straight into `bounds` — which places the card and nothing inside it, so with children the × had never been laid out and could not be clicked (its test caught this). It now lays each toast out with the engine at the origin and `shift_subtree`s it into its slot — the move `ContextMenu` and the command palette already make.

**5. The per-kind sweep's narrowest probe: 24px → 32px.**
A box is never narrower than its own padding — box model, not a defect: a card padded 13 a side has a 26px floor. **Verified this costs the sweep nothing**: with the layout rule disabled, all five original escapes still show at 32px.

═══ VERIFIED ═══
- The allowlist is EMPTY and `no_kind_paints_outside_the_box_it_is_given` passes.
- `the_catalog_paints_nothing_outside_the_window_it_is_given` runs WITHOUT `#[ignore]` and passes at 1400 / 900 / 600 / 320px.
- Full gate green: `./scripts/lint-changed.sh test` (1400+ tests, 0 failures, 0 ignored), then `./scripts/lint-changed.sh` — one PRE-EXISTING clippy warning in `key_hint.rs:484` (doc indentation, file untouched here).

═══ ⚠️ NOT VERIFIED — ANTONIO DRIVES THIS ═══
- Narrow the window hard: a dock header, a group header, a toast and a list row keep their text inside their own frames.
- **The toast is a rewrite of a widget's insides.** Its look and its hover/press.
- **One deliberate colour change**: the body line is now the theme `muted` token instead of the computed blend `foreground.lerp(muted, 0.2)`, so it reads slightly dimmer.
- With no leading icon the empty slot still costs one gap (the placeholder shape `Item` uses), so a no-icon toast's text starts ~10px further in than before.

═══ ROUND 2 — after Antonio's first look at the showcase (2026-08-25) ═══
Two defects reported, both real:

**a) The action button spanned the whole card.** A column stretches its children across the full width — right for the title and the body, wrong for a button. It now hugs its label (`align_self(Start)`), with a painted-scene test asserting the face is narrower than half the card.

**b) Hovering a stacked toast lit up the page behind it.** Two separate causes, one fixed:
- FIXED — `ToastStack` passed **every** pointer move through (`Handled::No`) so controls behind it kept animating while toasts showed; the showcase's event loop even documented that as intended. A card occludes the points it covers — the same answer `overlay_occludes` already gives a host — so a move that lands on a card is now consumed. Moves between and outside the cards still fall through.
- NOT FIXED — **the stack keeps its cards outside the component tree** (its own reconciled list, positioned by hand, input routed by hand in `on_event_capture`). The framework's hover pass never reaches inside a card there, so a **stacked** toast's action face and × do not light under the pointer; an inline toast in an ordinary tree does. This is a regression from the composition: the old card tracked hover itself from the delivered move. **The fix is to make the cards real children** — the engine then lays them out, hover and presses route themselves, and roughly 150 lines of hand-layout, hand-routing and hand-occlusion go with it. Feasible: the host lays the overlay root out every frame (`showcase.rs` :2739), so the stack has a viewport and `on_layout` to place them in. **Not started — it is a redesign of the widget and Antonio has not agreed it.** Recorded in `docs/widgets.md` under ToastStack as a known gap.

**Docs (AGENTS.md makes these mandatory with the change, and they were missing from round 1):** `docs/widgets.md` now carries the two layout rules the engine applies for every widget, the Toast entry's "content is children" section (cut-not-moved text, hugging action, published tone, who takes a press), and the ToastStack occlusion note plus the known gap. Rustdoc was written with the code.

**⚠️ FLAGGED, needs a decision — `toast.rs` is 531 lines**, over AGENTS.md's 400-line aim, and it is now a composition rather than one painted picture. § 0.3 says flag and agree the split rather than reorganise it unasked. Proposal: `widgets/toast/` with the card, its severity vocabulary and the stack as one file each.

**Also found, filed as T482:** every `DockFrame` reports its accessible name as the decorative drag grip `⠿` instead of its title, so the app prints a duplicate-name warning at startup and no dock's cursor position or hint letters survive a rebuild. Pre-existing; nothing here touched naming.

---
**Completion summary:**
DONE — verified by Antonio in the showcase, 2026-08-27 ("works fine").

The code was complete on 2026-08-25; this task only ever waited on eyes. What shipped is unchanged from the description above: the central `min_width: 0` layout rule (giving way is not optional once a row is out of room) which fixed three of the four escaping kinds with no widget touched; `Scene::draws_outside` replacing two hand-copied clip walks that were wrong the same way; the per-kind sweep with an EMPTY allowlist; and the catalog sweep running WITHOUT `#[ignore]` at 1400/900/600/320px.

WHY VERIFICATION TOOK A SECOND ATTEMPT — worth keeping
The first narrow-width pass looked broken: dock rows painted on top of each other, and nothing on screen after reopening. That was NOT this task. Two unrelated defects were masking it, both found by this very check and both since fixed centrally:

1. A dock or group toggle applied `hidden` on a CLICK — outside any layout pass — so every row kept the bounds it already had and was painted where it used to be. The framework had no way for a widget to say its TREE changed rather than its pixels. Fixed by `Base::mark_needs_layout` + `needs_layout(root)` (the layout twin of the damage walk), then properly centralised as `Base::set_hidden(bool)`, which sets and asks in one call and only asks when the value actually changed (safe inside `remeasure`). All 13 hand-written `style.layout.hidden` writes converted; a test fails the build on the raw form.
2. Clicking a row asked to be scrolled into view, so the region centred it and ate the click — only a second click did what the user meant. The library already documents "pointing at something never scrolls it"; it just had four copies of `focused` meaning "reveal me". Fixed by one definition, `Base::focused_by_keyboard()`, read by both the focus ring and the reveal.

Neither was reachable by tests — both needed Antonio driving. That is what this check is for.

- The one gap this task documented is `P096/T486` — now DONE: the stack's cards are real children, so hover and pick letters reach inside them.
- The `⠿` dock-naming defect found alongside it is `T482`, still open.

tasks.title: A dock is called '⠿' — its decorative drag grip answers the accessible-name walk before its title
tasks.description:
FOUND 2026-08-25 while verifying T481. Antonio sees it printed at every app start:

```
[heca] chrome: 2 unkeyed children of the root are all called '⠿' — give each one .key(its own id) or their cursor position and hint letters will not survive a rebuild
```

⛔ **THE ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS IN THIS TASK WAS WRONG — DISPROVED 2026-08-26. Read this before doing anything.**

It said: the dock's decorative drag grip is a literal `⠿` in a `Label`, a `Label` answers the accessible-name walk, so a dock is named after its grip; make the grip silent and the docks become distinguishable. **All of that is true and none of it fixes the warning.** What was actually tried and what happened:

1. Grip → `Icon` (silent). The warning came back as `▾` — the chevron, the next literal character in a label. **Renaming only moves which decoration answers.**
2. Chevron → `Icon` too. Not kept: Antonio said *"restore the grip anyway"*, and both were reverted. `dock_frame.rs` is untouched on the branch.
3. The dock's key handed down to its header row (the walk stops at the first node that is keyed **or actionable**, and a dock's header row is the actionable one). Warning unchanged.
4. A default identity from the dock's title when no key is declared. Warning unchanged. Reverted with the rest.

**MEASURED, not reasoned** (`heca/src/providers/workspaces/testing.rs` — `testing::Fixture` + `DockView { tree, scroll, focused }.build(&seams, &mut reg)`, which needs no window): building **two** seatings of the workspaces dock, with **two** workspaces, and running `heca_grid_ui::nav::ambiguous_identities` over the pair reports **nothing**. The workspace docks are already keyed `ws:{idx}` and are **not** the offenders. Every fix above was aimed at the wrong nodes.

═══ WHAT IS ACTUALLY KNOWN ═══
- **Identity is a path.** `nav::identity_of` collects the key of every keyed ancestor on the way down, so `key` is React's `key`: unique **among siblings**, scoped by the tree (`docs/widgets.md` § "The rule: two cases, and only two").
- **Antonio's reading, 2026-08-26:** *"this occurs because we have 2 same sidebar that are rendered on the screen creating duplicate"* — the same container tree rendered in the left and the right region. The duplication is therefore the **two region shells**, which declare no key, and the only name the walk can derive for either is the first text inside it: a dock's grip.
- The check runs on the **freshly built** chrome tree (`chrome/scene.rs` → `identity::report_ambiguous_widgets("chrome", &root)`), *before* any layout pass — so an identity assigned during `remeasure`/`on_layout` is invisible to it. That is why attempt 3 changed nothing.

═══ THE FIX TO TRY (proposed, agreed in principle, NOT applied) ═══
Key each **region shell** from the `RegionId` it is being built for — `chrome/scene.rs`, where `left_sidebar` and `right_sidebar` are built and each already receives its `RegionId`. Then the two root children are distinguishable and every identity inside becomes region-scoped: `left → ws:0` versus `right → ws:0`.

That second half is a live bug independent of the warning: two docks in two sidebars currently claim **one** identity, so a cursor position or a hint letter in the left sidebar is the same identity as the right one.

Antonio stopped the work here (*"we are doing too much with this sidebar"*), so this is proposed, not decided.

═══ VERIFY ═══
- Start the app: no `unkeyed children … called '⠿'` line. **Only Antonio can run this** — reproduce headlessly first with the fixture above, and do not ship another guess that needs him to re-run.
- A dock's cursor position and hint letters survive a chrome rebuild, and the left and right sidebars keep separate ones.

tasks.title: The showcase teaches developers to hand-roll a row the app has as a component
tasks.description:
THE DEFECT
`heca-renderer/examples/showcase.rs:1672` builds its PANES dock rows with a ~90-line inline closure — nested `Flex`/`Visibility`/`Label`/`Icon` with hardcoded `6.0`, `10.0`, `12.0`, `with_alpha(5)`, `font_scale(0.8)`. The app builds the same row as a component: `PaneRow{..}.build(..)` in `heca/src/providers/workspaces/pane_row.rs`.

Two implementations of one row, and only one gets fixed. The showcase copy still carries defects already repaired in the app this week:
- TWO `Label`s for one title, toggled by `Visibility` (app: the name is built once — c4352ac / 33a702f).
- The `StatusDot` pinned into a 12px slot (app: the dot declares it never gives way, the pinned slot is gone).

Antonio also reports the showcase PANES dock breaking on collapse/reopen ("all the content overlaps"). NOT reproduced headlessly: a plain `DockFrame` collapsed and re-expanded is byte-identical to its starting layout, and the same inside a `ScrollRegion` re-clamps correctly. So the fault is in this composed row or in repaint/damage, not in `DockFrame`. Diagnostic that splits the two: when it is broken, resize the window — if it snaps right it is damage, if not it is layout.

WHY IT HAPPENED (not carelessness — arrangement)
`heca-renderer/Cargo.toml` depends on `heca-core`, `heca-config`, `heca-grid-ui` — NOT on `heca`. So the showcase CANNOT import `PaneRow`. Whoever wrote the demo had one option: rebuild it by hand. The rule was not ignored; obeying it was impossible.

DESIRED (this task)
Drop the hand-rolled row. Keep the `DockFrame` demo itself — it is honest — with real widget children, so a developer reading the showcase sees a dock composed correctly instead of an invitation to hand-roll one. The showcase exists to show how to implement; a drifted copy is worse than no demo.

NOT THIS TASK
The real fix is extracting the row's domain-neutral presentation (status dot / icon / title / metadata line) into a `heca-grid-ui` widget both surfaces mount, leaving the app component to bind only the pane id and its intents (AGENTS.md § 0b: if it can be built inside grid-ui, it belongs there). That is a separate proposal and needs Antonio's agreement on the widget's shape.

  **through transparent wrappers** (`Visibility`, `KeyHint`, `Tooltip`) to the text inside — the case
  that was missed first time round. Three tests, including the wrapped one.
- **A selectable `Row` publishes its state colour**, as `Item` always did, so composed text follows
  selection. This is what removed the need to build a name twice.
- **`BASELINE_RATIO`** joins the two font-metric ratios the GPU-free layout side already assumes. If
  the UI font is ever swapped for one with different proportions, all three want revisiting together.
